539876|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 11% YoY to Rs 2,283 Cr, with EBIT margin exiting near 10% versus 6.8% in H1.
539876|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 11% YoY to Rs 2,283 Cr, led by 10% growth in ECD and 14% growth in lighting. Management said EBIT margin improved from 6.8% in H1 to about 10% in Q4, driven by operating leverage, premiumisation, pricing and cost optimisation. Consolidated EBITDA was Rs 271 Cr (11.9% margin). Butterfly returned to double-digit revenue and profit growth, and management took an impairment on its Butterfly carrying value, which is non-cash but hits ROCE and asset turnover. Management also announced a new super-premium product line, Crompton Rhion, and an identical dividend to last year.

financial_highlights.change: YoY, Q4; management called it industry-leading
YoY, Q4, with steady EBIT margins
Management says Butterfly is now cash flow positive

segments.name: ECD (Electrical Consumer Durables)
segments.commentary: Q4 growth of 10%, broad-based across pumps, small domestic appliances and fans. Fans saw record March volumes; BLDC portfolio growing 30%-plus. Management says it gained share in every ECD product in FY26 but did not give category numbers.

segments.commentary: Management said FY26 growth was in the early 20s percent and Q4 growth close to 30%, with a step-up in profitability. New launches included infrared cooktops, air fryers and premium juicers.

segments.name: Lighting (B2B and B2C)
segments.commentary: Q4 growth of 14%. Government share of B2B mix fell about 500 bps in FY26. Y-o-Y margin said to be roughly flat despite materially higher ad spend in the quarter.

segments.name: Butterfly Gandhimathi
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up 17% with steady EBIT margins and higher advertising spend. Management says it is back to strong double-digit growth in both revenue and profit, and an impairment was taken on its carrying value.

segments.commentary: Solar pumps revenue was about Rs 200 Cr last year and grew significantly this year. Rooftop order book is about Rs 500 Cr (about 38,000 units in Andhra plus Telangana), with about 5,000 homes installed so far. Management targets a Rs 2,000 Cr solar business in 3-4 years (corrected from Rs 1,500 Cr).

segments.commentary: Launched in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka and now selling in South India; national rollout is planned over the year rather than all at once.

guidance_outlook: Management expects margins to recover over time as input-cost turbulence from the war eases, but would not give a timeline.
Management said further material cost inflation came in April; it plans to offset this through pricing and Unnati cost actions, and says some benefits could be back-ended.
Dividend declared identical to last year.

Butterfly will focus on gaining traction in North, East, West (NEW) markets in the coming year.
Water heater BEE norms from July: management said it is fully prepared, with some cost increase to mitigate or pass on.
capex_capacity: Annual R&D and innovation spend about Rs 100 Cr, per management.
Rhion super-premium PL created; the Large Kitchen Appliance business folds into it; about 70 EBOs already operating.

Wires rollout ramping from Tamil Nadu and Karnataka to other states over the year.
Solar rooftop execution stepped up in the last 2-3 months.
demand_pricing: Two price increases in ECD since the war began, ahead of competition; about 7-8% cumulative price increase in fans in FY26, mostly taken in Q4.
Management said cost inflation continued into April; a war room tracks costs weekly or daily.
Butterfly has taken price increases similar to ECD's.
Residential pumps demand was tepid due to heavy rain; management says it held share. Agricultural pumps grew in the teens after product launches.
Air cooler inventory was cleared in the season; management says it gained marginal share. Water heaters were among the top 2 players in GT, now said to be No. 2.
Management says traditional-trade debtors are flat YoY and solar pump collections are on expectation; no stress seen so far in builders or contractors.

qa_highlights.question: What price increases were taken against the cost inflation, and how much has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Two ECD price increases since the war began, ahead of competition; about 7-8% cumulative in fans in FY26, mostly in Q4, which offset material inflation. Further inflation came in April, and management is waiting to see before deciding pricing for the rest of Q1 and Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 contribution and FY27 ramp-up from solar pumps and rooftops?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar pumps grew from about Rs 20 Cr three years ago to about Rs 200 Cr last year, and grew strongly again this year. Rooftop order book is about Rs 500 Cr, with about 5,000 homes installed. Management declined to give an FY27 contribution estimate.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lighting margins dip, and is growth troughing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins were roughly flat YoY despite higher ad spend. Growth came from a shift away from government B2B contracts (down about 500 bps), a higher-ASP B2C mix (panels, floodlights) and a reset supply chain and cost base.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Butterfly impairment's tax impact and is the merger still planned?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said there is no tax angle and it is an accounting impairment, not a write-off. Management said the impairment is unrelated to the merger plan, which remains on the cards at the right time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the national rollout plan for wires?
qa_highlights.answer: Launched in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, with ramp-up across the country over the year and distribution via the full Crompton network. No specific revenue targets given.

qa_highlights.question: Is there channel or payment stress in the value chain?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said traditional-trade debtors are flat YoY, solar pump collections are on track, and FY26 operating cash flow crossed Rs 500 Cr. Management said builder and contractor exposure is small and no stress is seen so far.

539876|2026-09.headline: Crompton Q2 FY27 revenue rose 18.2% YoY to Rs 2,263 Cr and EBITDA 24.1% to Rs 205 Cr, with margin up 40 bps to 9%.
539876|2026-09.overview: Crompton delivered its third straight quarter of double-digit revenue growth, with all business segments growing double digits per management. Revenue rose 18.2% YoY to Rs 2,263 Cr and EBITDA rose 24.1% YoY to Rs 205 Cr at a 9% margin. PBT excluding exceptional items grew 36.2%; the prior-year quarter carried a Rs 20 Cr Baroda plant restructuring exceptional, which inflates reported PAT growth of 65%. Management said price increases of about 80% of cost inflation have been passed through, supply disruptions from Q1 are over, and inventory days are back to year-ago levels. E-commerce was subdued due to a channel repositioning, and A&P spend was lower in H1.

segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 298 Cr, up 14.3% YoY, driven by B2C ceiling and outdoor lights and B2B industrial and indoor commercial. EBIT margin 12.9%, lower YoY due to pre-contracted B2B orders.

segments.commentary: Revenue grew 15.9% YoY excluding an in-house mixer grinder sale in the base; growth was largely price-led. Management said the core business grew about 16%.

segments.commentary: Solar rooftop (B2C and C&I) is live in six to seven states; wires launched in South India in Q1 and extended to Punjab, Delhi NCR and Gujarat. Management described both as nascent.

segments.commentary: Restructured under Butterfly CBO Shweta Sagar, to leverage the Butterfly ecosystem. Management cited a prior EBITDA loss of Rs 16-25 Cr for the business.

segments.commentary: Grew more than 70% YoY to a record quarterly revenue, led by fans with pumps, LDA and SDA also exported; markets are Africa, Middle East and South Asia. Margins are slightly lower than domestic, but sales are on cash terms.

539889|2026-03.headline: Parag Milk Foods Q4 FY26: gross margin rose to 28% from 25.9% in Q3, but EBITDA margin slipped to about 8.1% and core-category volumes fell 3%.

539889|2026-06.headline: Parag Milk Foods Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to INR945 crores (record Q1), but EBITDA margin slipped to 7.4% from 7.7% and PAT fell 20%.
539889|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue reached a record INR945 crores, up 11% YoY in value and 3% in volume. EBITDA grew 6% to INR70 crores, with margin down 30 bps to 7.4%; PBT was broadly flat and PAT fell 20% on higher current tax. Gross profit rose 11% to INR258 crores with gross margin stable at about 27.3%, which management attributed to calibrated pricing and mix. Flagship categories (ghee, cheese, paneer, dahi; 61% of revenue) saw volume fall 2% YoY, with B2C growing and B2B declining modestly; new-age business (Pride of Cows and Avvatar) grew 59% and reached about 13% of revenue.

financial_highlights.change: +11% YoY; gross margin stable (27.3% vs 28% in Q4 FY26 per call)

segments.name: Flagship categories (ghee, cheese, paneer, dahi)
segments.commentary: 61% of Q1 revenue; volume down 2% YoY on transient slowdown in certain channels, value up 10%. B2C grew strongly while B2B declined modestly; B2C flagship growth was 'high single digit to close to double digit'. Dahi now included in flagship (previously in Others).

segments.name: New-age business (Pride of Cows, Avvatar)
segments.commentary: Grew 59% YoY, about 13% of revenue vs 9% a year earlier. Portfolio expanded into protein bars, ready-to-drink (RTD) coffee with 15 g protein per serving (launched Q1), creatine. Management said new-age margins are roughly double the company average, without giving a figure.

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: Down 46% YoY per analyst question; management said this reflects PSI and state incentive income falling after GST cut on ghee and cheese from 12% to 5% in September 2025, plus dahi moving into flagship. UHT and beverages performed reasonably well.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 revenue growth above 10%, with Q2 and Q3 supported by festive demand.
Calibrated price increases will continue in response to commodity costs; ghee prices were raised late in Q1 and new-age prices were revisited recently.
Milk prices described as stable; slight increase possible in coming months due to monsoon-linked seasonality and festive demand.
Distribution target of more than 1.5 million outlets within three years.
Management aspires to return flagship B2C growth to double digits; B2B will be pursued where margins allow.
capex_capacity: Cheese capacity to double from 60 to 120 metric tons per day over about 1.5 years, targeted by March 2028.
Doubling cheese capacity to be paired with a parallel expansion in whey protein generation; milk procurement to be scaled up to match.
Renewable energy: a solar JV with Tata Power Solar; biogas power from farm (about 5,000 cattle); the investment value was INR4.6 crores per the annual report, not INR50 crores.
demand_pricing: Whey protein prices reportedly moved from about INR2,500/kg to about INR3,400/kg recently; management said global whey demand is structural, not temporary.
Management said Avvatar retail prices rose only in stages, not 100% as an analyst suggested; consumers switch between protein formats as prices change.
Q1 B2B volumes were deliberately forgone where customers negotiated hard on pricing, to protect margins.
Avvatar sales are 75% via quick commerce, e-commerce and website, and 25% via traditional retail and specialised protein outlets.
Management said Google searches and website traffic rose about 200% over the last two months, after the India's Got Latent association.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth break the roughly 10% sales growth band?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will exceed 10%, with Q2 and Q3 festive quarters expected to drive it; Q1 is seasonally weak.

qa_highlights.question: How is Avvatar up 59% when retail prices reportedly doubled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume also grew strongly and that prices rose in stages, not 100%; new products and lower-cost protein entry formats contributed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin flat despite mix improvement and price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said milk cost pass-through was complete in Q1 at INR42/litre, and the mix gain was offset by milk inflation; gross profit growth matched revenue growth at 11%.

qa_highlights.question: Why are core-category volumes falling despite wider distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is in B2B, where volumes were given up to protect profitability; B2C is not declining.

qa_highlights.question: Can B2B channel losses be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to name customers or channels or give numbers, citing commercial sensitivity; B2B deals are short-term and come and go.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Samay Raina / India's Got Latent deal's cost and ROI?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose cost, timeline or ROI, calling it a special commercial deal aimed at awareness.

qa_highlights.question: Is Avvatar's whey price rise a margin hit given backward integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose cost of production per kg or margin impact by product, saying margins are reported on a blended basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income spike in alternate quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income is usually higher in March due to annual fair-value gains on biological assets (cattle); Q1 FY26 also had a one-off gain on sale of the idle Sonipat plant.

risks_watch: Flagship volume decline (-2%) and B2B channel losses; watch whether B2C growth reaches double digits and offsets B2B.
EBITDA margin at 7.4% vs 7.7%, with brand media spend and Q1 seasonal absorption; watch for operating leverage in Q2 and Q3.
Tax-driven PAT decline (-20%); the current tax impact needs to be explained in future quarters.
Milk price stability versus monsoon and festive demand pressure, and dependence on price hikes for pass-through.
Other income is volatile (March fair-value gains; prior-year one-off), so the normalised base is unclear.
Cheese capacity doubling by March 2028 needs matching milk procurement.
Management declined to disclose new-age margin, category cost or Avvatar market share, limiting verification.

As a result, the gross profit increased by 11% to INR258 crores, in line with the overall revenue growth, demonstrating that the cost push has been passed on.

rows.why: Management set a target of more than 1.5 million outlets over three years, with B2C growing while B2B volumes are deliberately given up.

539889|2026-09.headline: Parag Milk Foods Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR1,241 crore, up 23% YoY, with volumes up 12% and EBITDA up 37% excluding last year's one-off.
539889|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue reached a record INR1,241 crore, with about half the growth from volume (12%) and the rest from price and mix. Gross profit rose 24% to INR323 crore and gross margin was 26% versus 25.8% a year ago, with gross margin per litre up from INR14 to INR17 despite milk costs rising about INR7 per litre. EBITDA excluding last year's FX MTM one-off was INR101 crore (8.1% margin, up 37%), and PAT grew 42% to INR42 crore. Net debt rose to INR678 crore from INR484 crore in March 2026, driven by inventory build-up from inflation and festive stocking, and management expects debt to stay in a similar range.

segments.name: Flagship categories (ghee, cheese, paneer, curd)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR778 crore in Q2, up 20% in value and 7% in volume. Paneer had its strongest volume quarter; ghee grew double digits in volume; Gowardhan holds 22% share in branded cow ghee.

segments.name: New Age (Pride of Cows, Avvatar)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR154 crore, up 71% YoY and 12% of revenue. Avvatar reports about 15% online whey protein share and over 75% of its revenue from quick commerce, e-commerce and its own website.

segments.name: Ingredients (MPC, lactose)
segments.commentary: Management said this segment grew exceptionally well in Q2, led by milk protein concentrate and lactose. No figures were given.

segments.name: Regions
segments.commentary: All four regions grew at high double digits; South and West were the fastest-growing. Regional disclosure was added this quarter.

guidance_outlook: Management expects high single-digit volume growth in core categories (paneer, ghee) in coming quarters, with no price increase planned in core categories.
Milk prices are not expected to soften in Q3 because of drought and deficient rains; procurement is at about INR46.5/litre and may hold through Q3.
Blended gross margin of 26-27% is expected to continue, with no dilution from new capacity.
A&P spend is expected to stay in the INR130-150 crore annual range; ~INR20 crore of Q2 spend is treated as non-recurring.
Net debt is not expected to fall materially; it may rise marginally as capex is funded. Management expects positive operating cash flow for FY27 as inventory unwinds.
New Age business targets a ~25% revenue share on the way to the INR10,000 crore ambition; management declined to give FY27 or FY28 growth numbers.
capex_capacity: Paneer: capacity rising 4x from 20 to 80 metric tons per day across Manchar and Palamaner, about INR100 crore, commissioning by June 2027; management expects about 80% utilisation soon after commissioning.

Cheese: capacity doubling from 60 to 120 metric tons per day for about INR105 crore at existing sites, phased 80, 100, then 120, with completion targeted for Q2 FY28; whey protein output doubles with it.
Combined capex of INR205 crore approved; management separately described a capex outlay of over INR200 crore for the year.
Board approved amalgamation of wholly owned subsidiary Bhagyalaxmi Dairy Farms into the company, subject to approvals.
Capex has been funded from internal accruals over the past three years; ECLGS 5.0 working capital funding and a new consortium lender were added this year.
demand_pricing: Two price increases were taken in the quarter; no further core-category price increase is planned.
Organised paneer share is low: management estimates 70-80% of out-of-home paneer is analogue, and about 4 million kg/day of paneer is consumed in India.
B2C grew double digits in Q2 and B2B was deliberately limited, as in Q1; overall mix is about 70% B2C and 30% B2B.
Management sees no price war from Milky Mist's capacity expansion (100 to 350 for paneer/cheese); it cites brand strength and distribution as its edge.
Management said blended gross margin is 26-27% and that cheese and whey are assessed together; no product-level margins are disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 7% flagship volume growth came from B2C festive stocking versus institutional buying, and how much of the INR177 crore other expenses is non-recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: B2C grew double digits in both Q2 and last year's Q2, and B2B was consciously limited. About INR20 crore of Q2 spend is one-off brand building; the rest is variable cost (power, fuel, supply chain) and A&P within an annual budget.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors view New Age growth and margins going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: New Age revenue reached INR154 crore in Q2 (INR118 crore in Q1, INR100 crore in Q4 FY26), an ARR above INR600 crore. Management did not give FY28 growth numbers but targets about 25% New Age share at the INR10,000 crore milestone.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for milk procurement cost in Q3 and Q4, given South cooperative price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Milk is at INR46.5/litre and is not expected to soften in Q3 because of drought. Karnataka's KMF raised prices, and some South response is possible; the South is 20-25% of procurement.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory and net debt high, and will cash flow turn positive by year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes the rise mainly to inflation and festive inventory; inventory days are stable. It expects the inventory build to unwind by year-end and believes FY27 operating cash flow will be positive.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin improvement, and how will the new cheese and whey capacity affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin per litre rose from INR14 to INR17 despite milk up INR7/litre; ingredients (MPC, lactose) grew strongly. Management says blended margin of 26-27% will hold as cheese and whey capacity doubles.

qa_highlights.question: What is the paneer and cheese capacity ramp, and what utilisation to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Paneer reaches 80 MT/day by June 2027 and could be about 80% utilised right away (roughly INR500-600 crore incremental revenue was suggested by an analyst). Cheese phases from 60 to 80 MT next month or so, then 100 and 120 MT by Q2 FY28; management assumes 80% utilisation.

risks_watch: Working capital and net debt (INR678 crore) are elevated; the company says FY27 operating cash flow should turn positive as inventory unwinds, which needs to be tracked.
Milk cost inflation: procurement at INR46.5/litre with no seasonal softening expected in Q3 because of drought; South cooperative price hikes could add pressure.
Other expenses rose to INR177 crore, including ~INR20 crore of brand spend that management calls non-recurring; A&P discipline is to be checked.
Capacity additions (paneer June 2027, cheese Q2 FY28) depend on demand absorption; new competitors such as Milky Mist are expanding paneer and cheese capacity.
Gross margin guidance of 26-27% is blended, and the company does not disclose product-level margins, which limits visibility into New Age and cheese economics.

key_quotes: Volumes grew by 12% this quarter, which accounts to about half of the increase and the remainder came from pricing and product mix.
We are increasingly seeing product availability and capacity determining the pace at which we can serve the market.
So I don't see any price war and all this things. It's only the ability to sell the brand, which we have and the distribution is very important.

539957|2026-03.headline: MGL Q4 FY26 net profit fell to INR132 crore from INR202 crore QoQ as West Asia LNG disruption curtailed industrial supply to about 80%.
539957|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 average sales volume rose 6.15% YoY to 4.672 mmscmd, with CNG at 3.349 mmscmd and DPNG at 0.605 mmscmd. Industrial and commercial supply was curtailed to about 80% from mid-March after the West Asia LNG disruption, and gas cost rose as the pooled gas mechanism replaced part of Henry Hub supply. FY26 EBITDA fell to INR1,451 crore from INR1,570 crore and PAT to INR847 crore from INR1,041 crore. Management declined to give firm FY27 margin guidance, saying it would prioritise volume growth and pass through costs only where alternate-fuel pricing allows.

qa_highlights.question: How much did March volumes fall, and what is the supply outlook for April and May?
qa_highlights.answer: Industrial supply (excluding commercial) fell by about 1.25-1.3 lakh scmd, roughly 20-22%, from a February average of about 5.75 lakh scmd. April was similar and May showed some improvement, and management did not guide on the pool mix.

qa_highlights.question: Is the gas cost increase covered by price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: DPNG's INR1 hike covers the APM increase. CNG has not been fully passed through, and management expects to absorb short-term volatility unless costs stay high.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for FY27 volume and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 volume growth could exceed 8% and could reach double digits if connections accelerate. It gave no firm margin number, but aims to stay above INR8 per SCM EBITDA, and said volume gets priority over margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why sign Brent-linked contracts when Henry Hub is cheaper, and why was HH cut in March?
qa_highlights.answer: Some Brent-linked contracts were signed earlier. HH was cut by force majeure and pooling, and management had no visibility on the pooling price or its end date.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CNG and DPNG growth outlook, and how does capex change?
qa_highlights.answer: Piped gas is expected to drive growth, with CNG at normal rates. Capex is guided at about INR1,200 crore, with some reorientation toward pipelines and lower RI costs.

539978|2026-06.headline: Quess Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue Rs 4,182 crore (+15% YoY) and PAT Rs 82 crore (+61% YoY), helped by a Rs 261 crore tax refund and a Rs 176 crore one-time Labour Code pass-through.
539978|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 15% YoY and 7% QoQ to Rs 4,182 crore, with all three core segments growing double digits on a YoY basis per management. EBITDA was Rs 85 crore (+21% YoY) at a 2.02% margin, while PAT of Rs 82 crore was boosted by other income from a Rs 261 crore income tax refund, including interest. Management attributed a one-time Rs 176 crore revenue pass-through to the new Labour Code, which it said did not add to profit. The company reported zero debt and a net cash position as of June 2026, and a final dividend of Rs 3 per share is pending AGM approval on 25 August 2026.

financial_highlights.change: +21% YoY; margin +11 bps YoY, -20 bps QoQ

financial_highlights.value: Rs 26 crore (incl. Rs 261 crore tax refund for prior years, Rs 22 crore interest)
financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 6 crore in Q4 FY26

segments.name: General Staffing
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 3,596 crore (+15% YoY, +8% QoQ), including the Rs 176 crore one-time Labour Code impact; EBITDA Rs 51 crore (+12% YoY, -2% QoQ). Net headcount added ~3,800 (about 5% growth in the quarter per analyst question), 86 new contracts, DSO 15 days AR, 37,000+ open mandates.

segments.name: Professional Staffing
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 252 crore (+3% YoY, +9% QoQ); EBITDA Rs 28 crore (+12% YoY) at ~11% margin. GCCs are 68% of revenue and 71% of headcount (headcount 7,129, +7% YoY); 36 new contracts and 1,100+ open mandates.

segments.name: Overseas
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 333 crore (+17% YoY, flat QoQ); EBITDA Rs 21 crore (+17% YoY) at ~6.2% margin. Malaysia revenue +55% YoY with 873 headcount; Middle East revenue +27% YoY at 12% EBITDA margin; Philippines revenue +17% YoY; 37 new logos added.

qa_highlights.question: Why is BFSI lagging, what is the Manufacturing margin profile versus BFSI, and what share of contracts is fixed vs variable markup?
qa_highlights.answer: BFSI recovery will take time given outsourcing regulation; Manufacturing PAPM is Rs 800-1,100 vs Rs 600-700 for GS overall. GS contracts are about 70:30 fixed to variable, with about 38% of Q1 new contracts variable.

qa_highlights.question: Is GCC hiring normalising, and is Rs 30 crore quarterly EBITDA (about 11.5-12%) achievable in Professional Staffing? What is steady-state GS margin ex the Rs 176 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: GCC share is 68% of revenue; management sees 250-300 new GCCs a year in India and only about 10% of the 2,407 captured. Professional Staffing margin guidance kept at 11-12%. GS margin would be a little over 1.5% after normalising for the Labor Code pass-through and April merit cycle.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Labor Code impact going forward and will it recur YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: About 68% of customers are covered YTD; full coverage expected by end-Q2 or early Q3. Remaining liability estimated below Rs 170 crore, about one-third of Q1; it is a pass-through with no profit benefit and is not expected to add significantly to revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ambition of reaching 1 million associates by 2030, and what role does M&A play?
qa_highlights.answer: The 1 million figure is a North Star; world No.1 requires about 125,000 more headcount. The model is capex-light partnerships, and no M&A is currently in the pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: How does Quess 2.0 economics compare with existing overseas and PS businesses, and what is the dollar-linked revenue base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give margin numbers before MSAs and delivery start; GCC revenue is about Rs 1.5-2.5 lakh per associate per month. Dollar-linked revenue is about 7% today.

qa_highlights.question: Are clients consolidating staffing vendors due to labour laws, and what is the sourcing and Japan corridor mechanism?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says policy changes have historically benefited the largest operator within 6-18 months; headcount has doubled from about 240,000 in March 2021 to 482,000. Japan corridor uses partners who are local, with about 5% of India's GCCs from Japan.

guidance_outlook: General Staffing: management targets 10-11% headcount growth per year (about 40,000-50,000 associates); about 5,000 added in Q1 FY27, and a net addition of 30,000-plus is the FY27 focus.

Labor Code: about 68% of customers covered YTD Q1; full coverage expected by end-Q2 or early Q3. CFO estimates the remaining one-time liability will be under Rs 170 crore (about one-third of the Rs 176 crore booked in Q1). Pass-through only, no EBITDA benefit.
Professional Staffing: guidance kept at 11-12% EBITDA margin, with internal priority of Rs 30 crore quarterly EBITDA run rate.
Overseas: EBITDA margin currently about 6.2-6.5%; guided to 6.5-7% as markets mature.
Quess 2.0: aspiration of 20-25% of revenue from higher-margin businesses over 3-4 years; profit-pool mix target of 65% from higher-margin and 35% from General Staffing.
Q2 outlook: management expects strong Q2 volumes from 86 new contracts, festive-season demand and 37,000 open GS mandates; no formal revenue or margin numerical guidance given.
capex_capacity: Capex-light, partner-led model for Quess 2.0 across five corridors (Japan, Israel, UK/Germany/Nordics, Canada/US); no new staffing companies or offices planned abroad.
Japan corridor signed and in execution (June 2026 go-live); Nordics/Europe in advanced discussion; Israel in discussion; North America at early exploration; four further partners not yet named.
Operating footprint: about 65 own offices, people deployed across 6,464 pin codes, 41% of associates in Tier-3 and below, 1,400 recruiters (about 750 dedicated to General Staffing).
No M&A currently in the plan; management said any value-accretive opportunity at the right valuation would be disclosed.
ELI scheme benefits not yet recognised in results.
demand_pricing: General Staffing: Rs 3,596 crore revenue (+15% YoY, +8% QoQ); growth led by Manufacturing and CRT (consumer, retail, telecom); BFSI declined marginally. Net headcount added about 3,800; 86 new contracts; 37,000+ open mandates; DSO 15 days (28 days including UBR).

General Staffing pricing: PAPM about Rs 600-700 broadly, Manufacturing Rs 800-1,100; gross margin about 2-3% in Consumer vs 5-6% in Manufacturing. Contracts are roughly 70% fixed and 30% variable; about 38% of new Q1 contracts were variable.

Professional Staffing: Rs 252 crore revenue (+3% YoY, +9% QoQ); GCCs 68% of revenue and about 71-72% of headcount; headcount 7,129 (+7% YoY); 36 new contracts; 1,100+ open mandates. Management cites 2,407 GCCs in India with Quess capturing about 10%.

Overseas: Rs 333 crore revenue (+17% YoY, flat QoQ); Malaysia +55% YoY with 873 headcount; Middle East +27% YoY; Philippines +17% YoY; 37 new logos. Overseas headcount about 7,000; about 7% of revenue is dollar-denominated, 93% INR.
Sourcing: about 46,000 gross additions in Q1 vs 29,000-30,000 a year earlier; about 18,000 joined payroll from sourcing in June alone.
Market sizing: management cites worldwide HR services of about $700 billion, Indian market about $19-20 billion where Quess is largest (9-10% share).
risks_watch: Labor Code liability: final number depends on customer choice between FTE and permanent models, and the remaining liability is expected by end-Q2; it can swing revenue QoQ.
BFSI weakness and regulatory limits on outsourcing could keep General Staffing growth concentrated in Manufacturing and CRT.
Overseas margin (6.2%) is below 10% and two markets are in double digits; visa and FTA timing for overseas and corridor plans is uncertain.
Quess 2.0 economics and partner identities remain undisclosed; the four unnamed partners and dollar-linked revenue ramp are unproven.
Profit-pool and PAT growth in Q1 were boosted by the Rs 261 crore tax refund, so underlying earnings growth is lower than headline.
GCC maturity may slow hiring in individual GCCs, and General Staffing flat-fee contracts can erode percentage margin.
key_quotes: Overall, the business performance has been broad-based, growth across every segment and I will just briefly talk about that.
Quess is no longer a volume organization, and I think consistently for five quarters in a row, we have shown that we are a volume and a value company.
The intention is not to have an operating staffing company in these countries because each of these countries have turned demographic negative more than 15 or 20 or 25 years ago.
So, we are so microscopically small there that it's not Quess people coming back to India.

539978|2026-09.headline: Quess Q2 FY27 revenue rose 15% YoY to INR4,396 crores, with PAT up 44% to INR75 crores, helped by a INR120 crore one-time Labour Code pass-through.
539978|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 15% YoY and 5% QoQ to INR4,396 crores, with adjusted EBITDA up 20% YoY to INR92 crores at a 2.1% margin. Reported PAT rose 44% YoY to INR75 crores, though it fell sequentially because Q1 included INR24 crores of one-time tax-refund other income. Headcount rose by a net 20,857 in General Staffing, and management said the add was concentrated in September. Professional Staffing margins fell to 10.5% on front-loaded IT Solutions investment, while management said gross margin in that segment grew 12% YoY.

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted EBITDA (excl. non-cash ESOP INR6 crores)

segments.name: General Staffing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR3,823 crores, +15% YoY (about +12% excluding INR120 crore Labour Code impact); EBITDA INR57 crores, +23% YoY. Net add 20,857 associates, 116 new contracts, record collections of INR4,285 crores, DSO 24 days.

segments.name: Professional Staffing (Quess IT Solutions)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR254 crores, +13% YoY; EBITDA INR27 crores, down 2% YoY, margin 10.5% vs 12.2% a year ago. 27 new contracts in Q2 (62 in H1); headcount 7,566 after net add of 437. Gross margin 20.5% vs 17.5% two years ago.

segments.name: Overseas
segments.commentary: Revenue INR318 crores, +10% YoY, -4% QoQ; EBITDA INR22 crores, +23% YoY, margin 6.9% vs 6.2% in Q1. Malaysia revenue +50% YoY, Philippines +15%; Middle East flat with 14.2% margin. 33 new contracts.

segments.name: Digital platform (BCPL)
segments.commentary: Turned EBITDA positive in Q2 after burn of nearly INR6 crores in FY26; paying clients rose from 14 in March to 54 in September. Management expects full-year FY27 breakeven.

guidance_outlook: General Staffing net additions guided at 10,000 to 15,000 per quarter as steady state; management said it may exceed this, and that things looked decent as of end-October.
Professional Staffing margin guidance of 11% to 12% for FY27, with exit near 12%; management said margin would have been 11.7% excluding the investment.
Labour Code one-time revenue: management sees no material residual impact in H2 FY27 (about 95-96% compliant at H1, 96.5% of payrolls done per Q&A).
Unallocated corporate cost (ESOP-related) expected at about INR20 crores in FY27, tapering to about INR15 crores in year 2.
Interim dividend of INR5 per share approved.
AI query system QMS targets answering half of associate queries by December 2026 and up to 80% by March 2027; Brain channel expects 35,000 to 40,000 offers in H2.
capex_capacity: Quess IT Solutions investment is strategic and multi-year (3 to 4 years), covering leadership, sales, delivery and practices; management compared it to FY21-22 investment that lifted EBITDA from INR31 crores to about INR110 crores run-rate.
Project Confluence (client sale to payroll, collections on one platform): Phase 1 goes live in January 2027, further phases in 2027.
Fractional workforce platform: first deal with a large FMCG brand for about 350 associates; full digital platform live by January 2027.
Open mandates in General Staffing stable at 30,000 to 35,000.
Global corridors: 135 workers mobilised to UAE in H1; MOU with IOM signed.
demand_pricing: Headcount about 504,000, +4% YoY and +5% QoQ; manufacturing added 7,800 associates in the quarter, with about 10 car makers as customers.
Gross margin in General Staffing and Professional Staffing both rose; PS gross margin grew 12% YoY, 3% QoQ.
PAPM steady at INR650 to 700; construction, VAS and manufacturing together are about 20% of mix, and higher-margin businesses are expected to lift PAPM over time.
Top-10 customers in Professional Staffing rose from 40% to 46% of revenue, with 62 new MSAs added in H1.
Management said the 80JJAA tax matter has four favourable precedents; hearing deferred from October to January.

qa_highlights.question: Why did General Staffing headcount add of 20,000 translate into only about 12% revenue growth excluding Labour Code?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said adds came late in the quarter, with about 65% in September and less than 33% in July-August, so revenue lags into Q3. It cited 116 new contracts and Brain sourcing as drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Will the mix shift to CRT and manufacturing sustain volume growth, and what does it mean for margins and collect-and-pay?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher-margin businesses (construction, VAS, manufacturing) are about 18-20% of mix; traditional flat-fee businesses are 80-82%. Collect-and-pay moved about 1% lower, which management attributed to customer mix; DSO was stable at 24 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Professional Staffing margin fall and what is steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment in IT Solutions drove the margin decline; ex-investment PS margin would have been 11.7%. FY27 guidance is 11-12%, exit near 12%. Top-10 share rose to 46%, and MSP declined due to one particular account.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the INR8 crore rise in unallocated corporate cost, and what is the trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to front-loaded non-cash ESOP accounting. FY27 expected at about INR20 crores, tapering to about INR15 crores in year 2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Labour Code residual impact and the EPF wage-ceiling effect?
qa_highlights.answer: No material residual H2 impact expected. The wage ceiling change from INR15,000 to INR25,000 raises employee contributions to about INR3,000 per month and slightly lifts revenue; management said 96.5% of payrolls were completed.

qa_highlights.question: Unbilled receivables and old receivables?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR300 crores of unbilled is from Labour Code provisions and will remain unbilled until employees are paid; the rest reflects 15% growth. The INR11 crore over-3-year item relates to ECL on unbilled revenue.

risks_watch: Revenue lag from late-quarter headcount adds; Q3 General Staffing revenue must show the flow-through.
Professional Staffing EBITDA margin at 10.5%, below the 12.2% year-ago level; recovery to 11-12% guidance is needed.
Pending EPFO demand of INR72 crores (no hearing date) and 80JJAA tax matter (hearing moved to January 2027).
Non-top-10 Professional Staffing customer revenue moderating; top-10 concentration at 46%.
Collect-and-pay share and higher-credit customer mix (15-30 day credit) could pressure working capital.

key_quotes: Our cash collection in this quarter was the highest ever, crossing INR5,000 crores.
Today, the contribution from the second half of this segment of the higher-margin businesses is nearly 18% to 20%, but the traditional businesses still continue to contribute around 80% to 82%.
An investment of this magnitude is not for the current financial year only. It is for the next 3 to 4 financial years.

539997|2026-03.headline: Kwality Pharma FY26 revenue rose ~36% to INR503 crore and PAT 69% to INR67 crore; FY27 guidance INR650 crore revenue and INR100 crore PAT reiterated.
539997|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 35.8% YoY to INR157.1 crore, with PAT of about INR25 crore. For FY26, EBITDA margin expanded from 22% to 24% and PAT margin from 10.8% to 13.4%. The cash conversion cycle improved from 208 to 170 days after Middle East payment delays of INR60-70 crore, of which about 40% had been realised by the call. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR650 crore revenue and INR100 crore PAT, and set FY29 target of INR1,000 crore revenue, with FY28 at INR800-850 crore.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR370 crore in FY25, ~36% growth
earlier years cited 55% to 48-49%; Q4 gross margin cited ~44.8% by analyst

segments.name: Oncology
segments.commentary: FY26 oncology revenue about INR100-120 crore (close to 20-25% of sales); projected INR150 crore in FY27 and up to INR300 crore by FY29. Peptide oncology EBITDA ~40%, routine oncology ~25%, blended ~30-32%.

segments.name: Unregulated/semi-regulated (legacy peptide, emulsion, liposome)
segments.commentary: Roughly 35% of FY26 sales, INR150-160 crore; expected to rise to INR200-250 crore in FY27-FY28 and ~25% of FY29 revenue.

segments.name: Domestic India
segments.commentary: Peptide-based products only, ~INR40-50 crore in FY26; management expects only 10-15% growth as no own marketing is done. About 5% of FY26 exports cited from India.

segments.name: Export regional mix (FY26)
segments.commentary: MENA 20%, GCC incl. Iraq/Kurdistan 25%, LATAM 30% (Mexico+Colombia 65-70% of LATAM), Southeast Asia 10-15%.

guidance_outlook: FY27: revenue INR650 crore (management sees INR650-700 crore) and PAT INR100 crore; upside from registrations in LatAm and high-regulated markets.
FY28: revenue INR800-850 crore at ~28% EBITDA margin; FY29: INR1,000 crore revenue at ~30% EBITDA margin. INR650 crore at 26-27% EBITDA margin.
FY29 INR1,000 crore excludes hormone and biosimilar revenue; management sees INR200 crore from these by FY29 as additional.
FY27 gross margin guided at 52-53% (vs 49% in FY26) as regulated sales start from Q2 FY27.
Quarterly FY27 path: Q1 INR150-160 crore, Q2 INR160-170 crore, Q4 above INR200 crore; ~15-20% QoQ growth.
Annual interest cost to stay ~INR11 crore; working capital not expected to rise materially; debtor days target 150-160.
capex_capacity: Oncology capacity utilisation rose from 30-35% to ~65% due to EU Annexure 1 changeover and validation timelines; ~INR50 crore expansion adding a line with three lyophilizers, fully automated.

Hormone Unit 6: ~INR65 crore capex, ~50% spent in FY26; target WHO GMP before November and commercialisation in ROW markets; target INR150 crore from unregulated/semi-regulated markets before FY29. Building for oncology and hormone complete.

Four projects (hormones, oncology expansion, biosimilars with clinical trials, R&D/BE): total INR260-270 crore, of which INR46 crore spent in FY26; INR90 crore planned in FY27 and INR90-100 crore in FY28.
Capex to be funded from operating cash flows in July-October; machinery payments 30-40% already made; 4-5 months to complete.
R&D: in-house R&D budget INR5-6 crore per year; outsourced R&D INR13-14 crore; clinical trials INR60-70 crore next year. R&D target 5-6% of revenue (from ~2%).
demand_pricing: Four registrations in Germany (high-regulated) expected in roughly the next two months; 3-4 of these could come in May as ministry queries were answered. Seven-eight regulated registrations expected by end CY2027, with ~40% EBITDA margins on fresh registrations.

LatAm: 55 submissions in FY26, ~10 approvals so far, ~6 more expected in Q1-Q2 FY27, all 55 targeted by end CY2027; 25-30 more submissions planned in FY27. LatAm to contribute ~30% of FY29 revenue, Algeria 15-16%, French West Africa ~10%, GCC 10-15%, Russia 5-7%.
Middle East: Algeria sales INR80-90 crore in FY26 and INR25-30 crore in Q4; GCC margins 20-25% and management plans to replace some GCC sales with bioequivalence products at 30-35% margins.
Raw materials: ~85% sourced in India, 15% from China; API prices not up much; rupee/dollar and euro movements offset cost increases; no plan to pass costs on currently.
Debtor days fell to ~170 (from 140-150 cited by analyst in one answer); MENA receivable exposure came from government tender supplies on 100% credit.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance of INR650 crore conservative given Q4 annualises to that level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is somewhat conservative; true range INR650-700 crore, with potential upside of ~INR50 crore on faster LatAm and regulatory registrations.

qa_highlights.question: Oncology FY26 revenue, margins and FY29 trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 oncology ~INR100 crore; FY27 INR150 crore and FY29 up to INR300 crore. Blended oncology EBITDA 30-32% (peptides ~40%, routine ~25%).

qa_highlights.question: How will margins expand from 27% to 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Driven by fresh regulated registrations at ~40% EBITDA, oncology mix, and bioequivalence products; margins on new off-patent products expected 40-45% initially, falling to 25-30% by FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and receivables recovery?

540005|2026-09.headline: LTM Q2 FY27 revenue rose 5.1% YoY in constant currency to USD 1.24bn, with order inflow of USD 1.3bn and EBIT margin at 15.6%.

EBIT margin expanded 10bps QoQ to 15.6%, while PAT margin fell to 11.7% from 12.7% because Q1 included a one-time gain on Voicing.AI. Cash conversion weakened sharply (OCF/PAT 39%, FCF/PAT 24%) due to gratuity funding under the labour codes, an ad hoc TDS timing effect, and advance tax. Order inflow of USD 1.3bn was AI-centric, short-tenure deals, and management is deliberately shifting KPIs away from TCV. Management reiterated that H2 will be better than H1, with the Saudi business (routed via a JV and classified under Tech) a drag this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth reach high-single or double digits by FY28, and is FY27 close to FY26?

qa_highlights.question: Is the top BFSI client's vendor spend cut a medium-term risk?

qa_highlights.question: Why is payout low versus peers, and what are capital allocation plans?

qa_highlights.question: Why is US growth lagging the market, and what is the reason for the about 14% decline in international Human Nutrition?

540047|2026-06.headline: DBL Q1 FY27 standalone revenue Rs 1,930 crore and EBITDA margin 10.32%; consolidated PAT fell to Rs 128 crore from Rs 271 crore.

Standalone PAT fell to Rs 39 crore from Rs 123 crore, but the base quarter included a Rs 98 crore divestment gain. Consolidated revenue dipped to Rs 2,378 crore from Rs 2,620 crore, with consolidated EBITDA of Rs 429 crore (18.05% margin). Management reiterated FY27 guidance (revenue growth 30-40%, EBITDA margin 10-12%, debt reduction Rs 600-800 crore) and announced a stake sale in under-construction transmission and solar projects (about Rs 8,400 crore project cost) to Alpha Alternatives.

qa_highlights.question: How much bid value is pending opening, and what is the working capital outlook?

Siarmal coal fee is 78% until the CHP is ready, rising to 100%, with a major revenue jump expected in FY29. Full-year math given as about Rs 600/t for Siarmal and Rs 1,200/t for Pachhwara.

Rs 7,801 crore consol net debt is referenced; the company cites Rs 45,000 crore of road HAM projects done.

qa_highlights.answer: Standalone other income was about Rs 40 crore: Rs 26 crore dividend from Alpha, about Rs 5 crore InvIT interest, and about Rs 9 crore FDR and other income. Standalone capex for FY27 stays under Rs 100 crore.

540048|2026-03.headline: S.P. Apparels Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue fell to INR 364 crore (from INR 399 crore) and EBITDA margin to 12.2%; management guides INR 2,000 crore FY27 revenue.
540048|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was soft on volumes: consolidated revenue declined year-on-year to INR 364 crore and EBITDA to INR 44 crore, with PAT down to INR 18.59 crore, as US tariff after-effects and shipping disruption delayed orders. Full-year consolidated revenue grew 13.2% to INR 1,578 crore and EBITDA rose 16% to INR 217 crore. Management says US orders are returning, guides to INR 2,000 crore consolidated revenue in FY27, and points to Sri Lanka ramp-up and EU/UK FTA benefits. Current utilisation is cited at 64%, and the timing of recovery in H2 FY27 is the key uncertainty.

segments.name: Young Brand Apparel
segments.commentary: FY26 adjusted revenue INR 321.26 crore and adjusted EBITDA INR 49.23 crore; Q4 adjusted revenue INR 66.88 crore (vs INR 81.37 crore) and adjusted EBITDA INR 8.47 crore (vs INR 12.85 crore). Business is 100% US-customer based and was hit by tariffs.

segments.name: SPUK (UK)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue GBP 7.5 million (INR 87.04 crore) with positive EBITDA of INR 1.10 crore. Q4 revenue was INR 35.04 crore vs INR 18.34 crore a year earlier. Order book is GBP 6.1 million.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 71.54 crore (vs INR 79.41 crore); EBITDA loss narrowed to INR 6.1 crore from INR 6.84 crore. Management says Retail was EBITDA-positive from Q2 to Q4 FY26, and that finance cost, not depreciation, keeps it PAT-negative.

540073|2026-03.headline: BLS International FY26 revenue rose 37% to INR2,998 crores and EBITDA 30% to INR819 crores, with Q4 PAT up 29% to INR187 crores.

Digital EBITDA margins are thin (about 7-8%) after the Aadifidelis loan-distribution mix shift, while Visa & Consular margins expanded to about 40%. 540097|2026-09.headline: GAMCO H1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 79% to INR254 crore and net profit reached INR38.5 crore, with Q2 PAT of INR6 crore.
540097|2026-09.overview: Consolidated H1 FY27 revenue from operations grew 79% to INR254 crore, already about 84% of FY26 full-year revenue, with EBITDA of INR52.9 crore and net profit of INR38.5 crore versus INR6.5 crore in H1 FY26. Q2 revenue rose 61.7% YoY to INR140.6 crore, but Q2 EBITDA of INR12 crore (9% margin) and PAT of INR6 crore were well below Q1, which management attributed to a one-off strong Q1. Net worth rose 24% in six months to INR206.6 crore and debt-to-equity improved to about 1.6x from 1.7x. Management framed the company as a four-vertical group (equity investments, real estate, logistics, hospitality) shifting from marketing gains toward asset-backed income, with most asset revenues expected from FY28 onward.

segments.name: Equity investments / treasury
segments.commentary: Quoted equity investment of about INR230 crore, including stakes in Swiggy, TrucksUp and Drivers4Me. Management said these listed holdings are the most liquid source of funding for expansion.

segments.name: Real estate (Kolkata, OneWorld)
segments.commentary: 9.7% stake in OneWorld, a 212-acre Lucknow township, invested at about INR19.4 crore and revalued at INR153 crore (unrealised gain about INR134 crore). Kolkata plans 13.5 lakh sq ft of residential launches over 1-2 years; Alipore (Uma Properties) expected to yield about INR250 crore revenue, and Jessore Road JV (Elika Realestate, 45% stake) about INR1,100 crore over 5 years.

segments.name: Warehousing / logistics
segments.commentary: Dankuni, Delhi Road land with 40 lakh sq ft development potential and about INR600 crore capex, targeting 8-10% rental yields. Calcutta 100-125 acre project to deliver 25-30 lakh sq ft; revenue expected from calendar 2028. Visco Advisory warehousing asset sold for INR15.8 crore.

segments.name: Hospitality
segments.commentary: Acquired 33.33% of Blissara Resorts (Port Blair) with INR69 crore post-money valuation; planning a 140-key upper upscale hotel on 11 acres with coastal clearance in place. Construction to start in about a month; revenue expected from about 2030 with 5.5-7 year payback including debt and equity.

demand_pricing: Management cited zero Grade A warehouse supply in Calcutta and limited hotel supply in Port Blair, Lucknow, Himachal and Ayodhya; no pricing or occupancy data were given.

Hotel valuation benchmark cited at 10-16x EBITDA; 40-45% GOP assumed for the hotel.
Management said the Port Blair hotel faces no competition for about 3 years after opening.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company expand into factoring, lease financing and security-backed lending, and how does this fit with real estate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would be selective and pursue structured niche deals, not plain-vanilla lending, citing the Shalimar Lake City (OneWorld) revaluation and the Visco Advisory exit as examples.

qa_highlights.question: Which vertical will create the most value over 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is most excited about hospitality, then warehousing, targeting INR100 crore revenue and INR500-600 crore valuation per hotel.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for hospitality and warehousing revenue, and what are the execution risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Blissara revenue starts around 2030 after construction; warehousing revenue from calendar 2028; Alipore residential from about March/April 2028. Monsoon delays were the main constraint, now considered over.

qa_highlights.question: How does revenue recognition work with the hotel operator, and what is the payback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the operator takes a 1.5-2.5% base fee on gross revenue plus a share of gross operating profit, with total fees under about 8-8.5%. Payback is about 5.5-7 years including debt and equity; INR69 crore post-money valuation for Blissara.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR900-1,500 crore funding requirement be met?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will use the listed equity treasury (keeping about 25% liquid), market borrowing for construction, internal accruals, and asset liquidation as needed. Management did not confirm the analyst's INR400 crore liquidation estimate.

qa_highlights.question: Who owns the other 55% of the Jessore Road project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said three or four other West Bengal real estate developers hold the remaining 55%, chosen for execution capability.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter hospitality as landowner/investor rather than operator, and how much control does GAMCO have?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it lacks operating experience and prefers global operators, and that development-stage entry captures higher returns (11-12% on Tier 2 land versus 7-9% for Tier 1 warehouses). It said it would provide guidance and strategic input.

540115|2026-03.headline: LTTS Q4 FY26 revenue rose 0.3% YoY to $305.9 Mn and EBIT margin reached 15.2%, with mid-16% margin targeted by Q4 FY27 or earlier.
540115|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 continuing-operations revenue was $305.9 Mn, up 0.3% YoY and down 1.7% QoQ, as the company exited low-margin work and divested SWC (Smart World). EBIT margin rose 40 bps QoQ to 15.2%, the second straight quarter of expansion, with gross margin up 150 bps QoQ. Management said the restructuring is complete, with about $19 Mn annualised revenue exited in Q4 and no further restructuring costs expected. It advanced the margin aspiration to mid-16% by Q4 FY27 or earlier and set a 5-year Lakshya 31 plan of 13%-15% USD CAGR and 16%-17% EBIT margin, with no annual guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 16%-17% margin a five-year target or achievable sooner?

qa_highlights.question: When will the 13%-15% CAGR show up, and when do $100 Mn+ and several-hundred-million accounts emerge?

qa_highlights.question: Is the 13%-15% CAGR in USD and does the 12.4% historical figure include SWC?
qa_highlights.answer: The 13%-15% is USD-based, and the 12.4% five-year CAGR includes SWC. Reported-currency targets may be added over time.

qa_highlights.question: How big are the six bets and what investment is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Less than 50% of revenue today comes from the six bets; more than 70% expected in five years. Management will hold an Investor Day later in the year with detail. Investment focuses on EI, SDV, connectivity, and physical AI.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be more restructuring, and what is the reason for the $19 Mn exit?

qa_highlights.question: Why did Tech decline QoQ, and what differentiates Mobility in a weak auto market?
qa_highlights.answer: Tech fell due to a medical program ending and a new one not starting on schedule; management expects Mobility and Tech to grow in FY27. Mobility differentiation was cited as EV/hybrid lab investments, SDV with AI, and diversification across auto, T&OH, Aero and Rail.

qa_highlights.question: Will AI-led large deal sizes and vendor consolidation appear in ER&D?

qa_highlights.question: Will FCF to net income stay at 153%?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Gupta said Q1 was a stellar working-capital quarter; the full-year FCF conversion expected is 90-95% of net income.

qa_highlights.question: Does AI-led productivity hit pricing, and how is it passed on?

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 growth be better than Q1?

qa_highlights.question: Is the Tech share of revenue structural, and what is the outlook for other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Gupta said Tech will not return to its 34% share soon; growth will come more from Sustainability and Mobility. Other income is lower mainly on hedge losses, and the same range is expected for the next few quarters.

EBIT margin widened 60 bps QoQ to 16.3%, and management said the mid-16% aspiration was reached a couple of quarters early. Large deal TCV was $203M with over 50% AI-led, and management said the USD100M shortfall from last quarter's target would be recovered over Q3 and Q4. Reported net income of INR 548 crore included a one-time INR 165 crore gain from the SWC divestment, which is now complete.

segments.name: Sustainability
segments.commentary: Up 13.4% YoY and 4.9% QoQ; now about 30% of revenue per the CFO (38% per the later AI-revenue answer, which conflicts). Nearly half of Q2 large deal wins were here. Margin 29.5%. Management says it is on track for another double-digit growth year.

segments.name: Tech
segments.commentary: Described as stable. Tech Infra and Semcon were strong, Media steady. A global telecom equipment AI program began ramping this quarter. Margin 12%, up 50 bps QoQ. Management expects Tech to be muted in Q3, with Medtech recovery in Q4.

segments.commentary: Annualized EI-led revenue of $120M in Q2, which management said is about 9.5% of revenue. Headcount was 24,035 and more than 16,000 engineers were upskilled in AI. Over 50% of Q2 large deal wins were AI-led.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 revenue expected to be better than H1, both QoQ and YoY, per management.
Near-term EBIT margin expected around mid-16% levels; aspiration to maintain it.

Wage hike effective Q3, expected impact of 50 to 80 bps on margin; margin guidance stated as inclusive of this.
Effective tax rate guided at 26% to 26.5%.

Offshore mix 55.9%; fixed-price mix 35.6%, rising toward higher-value and outcome-based engagements.
Average deal tenures have lengthened slightly. Management cited roughly 5 to 7 years for a $100M deal, 4 to 5 years for $50M, about 3 years for $25M.
Management says it charges a premium for AI-led work but declined to quantify AI-led margins by service line.
Rupee realized at 95.9 per dollar in Q2, depreciating 1.09% QoQ.
Attrition range-bound at 14.7%.
Europe auto remains weak; management said there is little Middle East exposure in oil and gas.

qa_highlights.question: How has Sustainability volatility come down, and how much revenue is long-term?
qa_highlights.answer: Management split Sustainability into four areas (Oil and Gas/Chemicals, FMCG, Energy Automation, Industrial Machinery and Building Tech), built digital twin and AI solutions, and said large deals from last year are now converting to revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Middle East situation affecting oil and gas or overall business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Middle East business is very small and it is not seeing significant impact; work is focused on the US and Europe.

qa_highlights.question: Will European auto recover next year, and is it an industry-wide turnaround?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Europe auto to stabilize in the next 6 to 9 months and grow again in 9 to 12 months, as European OEMs rebase and India-based providers replace local vendors. Auto Europe is about 50% of the auto portion of Mobility, and the company does not quantify it.

qa_highlights.question: Is the DSO of 78 days comfortable, or is there room to improve it?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the company is comfortable at 78 days, well below the 80 to 85 day guided range, and expects to operate around this level.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the SWC divestment affect the reported numbers, and what is the run rate from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the INR 165 crore was a one-time gain. From Q3 only continuing operations will be reported, with the SWC operating line of about $36M excluded.

qa_highlights.question: Why are clients converting deals to revenue now, and what changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to AI capex across chips, software, industrials, telecom and infrastructure, clients focusing on growth rather than cost cuts, and LTTS being 9 to 12 months ahead of peers on AI, which it says is gaining share.

qa_highlights.question: What are sustainable margins, and what is the Q4 exit margin?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said near-term margins should be taken at around mid-16% EBIT, with levers from mix, AI and productivity, net of the wage hike. Management did not give a Q4 exit margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wage hike impact, and what does H2 growth mean?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the wage hike in Q3 would have a 50 to 80 bps margin impact. Management said H2 will be better than H1 both QoQ and YoY, without a quarterly number.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the $120M annualized EI revenue was recognized in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the $120M is annualized, so about $30M per quarter. Most AI deal wins have not yet gone into operation, and the company will report AI-led revenue quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: How is AI-led revenue defined, and what is its profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: AI revenue counts deliverables where a significant part is created using the AI stack. Management declined to quantify AI-led profitability, but said AI is a margin lever.

540133|2026-03.headline: ICICI Pru Life FY26 VNB rose 10.9% to ₹26.29bn with margin up 190bp to 24.7%, but APE grew only 2.2% and RoEV fell to 11.9%.
540133|2026-03.overview: FY26 showed absolute VNB growth of 10.9% to ₹26.29bn and VNB margin expansion to 24.7% (from 22.8%), while APE grew just 2.2% to ₹106.41bn. Retail protection was the standout, up 32.3% for the year and 60.5% in Q4, offsetting weak agency, direct, linked and annuity lines. Profit after tax rose 34.6% to ₹16bn, helped by a ₹1.14bn gain on sale of ICICI Pension Fund Management Company; excluding it, PAT grew 25%. EV operating assumption changes (GST input-tax-credit loss, persistency) and a ₹2.64bn persistency variance (mainly the 100% premium back annuity) pulled RoEV down to 11.9%. Management said West Asia disruption hurt March new business across all lines except protection, and it deferred Ind-AS adoption by a year via forbearance.

segments.name: Retail protection

segments.name: Group protection
segments.commentary: Up 7.1% YoY; group term +14.6%, credit life +1.8%. Group business overall +14.5%, 18.3% of APE.

segments.name: Linked (ULIP)
segments.commentary: APE up 1.6% YoY; two-year CAGR 14.2%. Focus on high sum assured ULIP to cushion market volatility.

segments.name: Non-linked savings
segments.commentary: APE grew 15.4% YoY for nine months but declined YoY in Q4 as a prior-year Q4 launch normalised; full year roughly flat. Par:non-par roughly 2:1.

segments.name: Annuity
segments.commentary: Four-year CAGR about 20%; stabilised at about 7% of retail mix. Heavy single-pay skew and 100% premium back product drove persistency issues.

segments.name: Group Funds
segments.commentary: Grew 26% YoY.

segments.name: Agency channel
segments.commentary: APE ₹26.86bn; with direct, 47.4% of retail APE. Growth weak on high annuity base, but improving sequentially through the year.

segments.name: Direct channel
segments.commentary: APE ₹14.30bn; growth lagged on base effects. Focus on NRI via GIFT City and online channel.

segments.name: Bancassurance
segments.commentary: Grew 3.6% YoY; 29.8% of APE. 53 bank partnerships with access to 26,400+ branches.

segments.name: Partnership distribution
segments.commentary: Grew 23.4% YoY; 13.2% of APE. Over 1,500 non-bank partnerships.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 growth number given; management called the environment volatile and said it is too early to commit.

Management said VNB margin of 24.7% (with persistency and mortality/expense assumptions now set) is the baseline going forward.
Ind-AS go-live deferred by a year via forbearance; current-year results remain on existing I-GAAP with Ind-AS as alternate financials.
Would reprice non-par products if the yield curve moves down; no en masse repricing so far, only cohort-level changes (1-3% at some peers).

Management said it has not cut prices en masse; the yield curve benefit was retained rather than passed to customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 growth strategy and non-par outlook, and what is the par/non-par mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth outlook not committed given volatility. Par:non-par mix roughly 2:1 for the year, with some quarters higher or lower.

qa_highlights.question: Is the persistency experience built into VNB margin assumptions, and what about surrender value regulation?
qa_highlights.answer: Persistency is reviewed at year-end; permanent changes go into assumptions and temporary ones run through variances. Early surrender-value product experience is not yet showing a material difference after 5-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is agency growing slowly, and how will it be revived?
qa_highlights.answer: Agency was held back by a high annuity base in the prior year. The 3-year CAGR is about 12-13%; micro-market-led agency strategy is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Did the West Asia war affect new business, and how does demand differ across products?
qa_highlights.answer: March new business was hit across the board except protection. Management declined to quantify the impact.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Ind-AS transition plan and its capital impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Forbearance sought for one year, citing awaited joint expert group clarity on CSM inputs. Solvency stays on the existing basis (227%) until RBC is implemented.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 2.5pp economic variance uplift in VNB margin, and was pricing changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Yield curve gains were held in economic assumptions, while product repricing sits in new business profile. Pricing was not materially changed; cost efficiencies were used to hold prices.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the EV split between VIF and net worth reclassified?
qa_highlights.answer: Shareholder share of MTM on policyholder-fund assets and derivatives moved from net worth to VIF to align with market practice. Total EV is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2.64bn persistency variance related to FY26 VNB?
qa_highlights.answer: Almost none of it relates to FY26 business; it is entirely back-book.

qa_highlights.question: Any update on commission regulation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is not aware of discussions beyond data requests from the regulator; distributor remuneration talks are continuous.

540133|2026-06.headline: ICICI Pru Life Q1 FY27: VNB up 24.9% YoY to ₹5.71 bn at 26.7% margin, driven by retail protection growth of 60.4%.
540133|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 VNB grew 24.9% YoY to ₹5.71 bn, with VNB margin at 26.7%, up 200 bps from FY26's 24.7%. PAT rose 27.8% YoY to ₹3.86 bn. Growth was led by protection: sum assured up 31.8% to ₹4.90 trn and protection APE up 45.7%, while savings APE rose only 5.8% and non-linked APE fell about 9.5% as fixed deposits attracted customers. Management repeatedly stated there is no margin target and no formal guidance, and that absolute VNB growth is the focus.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the VNB margin, and is the GST input tax credit drag still affecting it?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Dhiren Salian said the margin was largely product mix; the non-availability of input tax credit continues for one more quarter (Q2) before entering the base from Q3. He did not quantify the drag.

qa_highlights.question: Why is non-par not selling, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed-income alternatives, mainly fixed deposits with high sticker rates, are more attractive to customers. Non-par is not being avoided and is repriced as conditions allow, but the pickup depends on those alternatives easing.

qa_highlights.question: Will Standard Chartered remain an open-architecture partner after Prudential's change in promoter status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Standard Chartered has been a 10-year partner, that both sides value it, and that ICICI Bank is the largest single channel at about 15% of business with no other distributor above 5%.

qa_highlights.question: How does expense management look, and what is the ITC drag in rupees?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost-to-premium is up on the input tax credit loss, partly offset by productivity and AI/ML gains. It did not quantify the ITC impact and said the schedules would show the GST component. It said EOM is well within the cap, without disclosing the figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any VNB growth guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management declined to give VNB growth guidance, including the 20-25% range an analyst proposed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Prudential promoter-to-investor reclassification?
qa_highlights.answer: Prudential holds just under 22%. The board approved its request to reclassify as investor, and the company has submitted it to IRDAI, awaiting its response. Management said no sell-down is required under its reading of the rules.

540133|2026-09.headline: H1-FY27 VNB rose 22.3% to ₹12.83 billion, with VNB margin at 26.0% on a protection-led mix shift.

Consumer and Industrial (C&I) grew 26% to Rs 784 crore and rose to 43% of revenue from 37%, led by wires and cables (up 50% to Rs 340 crore). Smart metering recovered from an industry-wide execution disruption earlier in the year, with Q4 its strongest quarter, and the order book stood at over Rs 3,200 crore (over 97% metering) as of 22 May 2026. Management flagged C&I margin pressure in FY26 from mix shift and a lag in passing on commodity-linked price increases, which it expects to ease from late April and May.

540136|2026-09.headline: HPL Electric Q2 FY27 revenue rose 40% YoY to ₹608 crore, a record, but EBITDA margin slipped to 11.74%.
540136|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations grew 40% YoY to ₹608 crore, the first quarter above ₹600 crore, taking H1 revenue to ₹1,124 crore (up 37%). Consumer and Industrial (C&I) revenue grew 64% to ₹337 crore and was about 55% of quarterly revenue, while Metering and Systems grew 18% to ₹271 crore. Q2 EBITDA rose 8% to ₹71 crore and PAT rose to ₹23 crore, but the EBITDA margin fell to 11.74% from 12.26% in Q1 on input cost inflation and mix. The Board also gave in-principle approval to evaluate a restructuring, possibly a scheme of arrangement to separate one or more businesses.

segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹178 crore, up 159% YoY; H1 ₹324 crore, about 95% of FY26 full-year revenue. Growth is now mostly volume-led, with telecom, real estate, retail, panel builders and OEMs cited as drivers.

segments.name: Lighting and switchgear (within C&I)
segments.commentary: Lighting grew 59% YoY, domestic switchgear 43% YoY, and industrial switchgear 29% QoQ. Management plans a revamped lighting range around ELECRAMA in February; fans are a new category with pan-India launch targeted for summer 2027.

segments.name: Metering and Systems
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹271 crore, up 18% YoY and 14% QoQ; H1 ₹509 crore, up 17%. Order book of ₹2,700 crore gives visibility beyond the current year, though quarterly conversion depends on customer schedules.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins normalise in the second half, and what is the full-year margin outlook?

H2 FY27 expected to be much better than H1; C&I to comfortably exceed the ₹1,000 crore indication (already ₹615 crore in H1); FY28 sales plan almost ready.

540153|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated total income rose 37.3% YoY to ₹4,116 crores, with EBITDA margin at 14.5%, while raw-material and energy inflation remain a pass-through challenge.

Consolidated Q4 EBITDA rose 30.8% to ₹598 crores, helped by Europe's best-ever quarter (EBITDA €21.9 million, 20.5% margin). Management said full-year standalone RMC rose 1.5 percentage points to 66.82% of revenue, and that ₹73.7 crores of aluminium and steel inflation was not passed through, which would have lifted FY26 EBITDA margin to 13.3% from 12.6%. Management expects Q1 FY27 to stay volatile on energy and metal costs and sees better numbers from Q2.

rows.why: Maharashtra PSI incentive rises to ₹858 crore total with ₹75 crore booked in H1 and about ₹50 crore expected in H2 FY27, and Maxwell's margin is targeted to turn double-digit in FY28, but no revenue or margin guidance raise was made.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Standalone RMC is at 70% of sales (vs 66%) and the Q3 RMC reduction depends on pass-through that only some customers agreed to, while management expects steel prices to rise; greenfield plants carry about a 0.5% negative PBT margin drag in Q2.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Battery pack SOP ramp for a leading 2W OEM completes in Q3 FY27, two PV OEM battery pack nominations start Q1-Q2 FY28, and the Sanand solar actuator SOP is in Q4 FY27 with US solar SOP in H2 FY27.

rows.label: Proprietary 4W and non-auto SOP ramp to FY31
rows.why: Targets are 4W SOPs of ₹100 crore in FY28 rising to ₹800 crore in FY31, non-auto SOP of ₹250 crore in FY28 rising to ₹650 crore by FY31, and proprietary 4W above ₹1,500 crore by FY31, though management says this is not achievable within two years.

rows.label: EU import caps and local-content rules
rows.why: A 350,000-unit cap on Chinese plug-in and mild hybrid imports starts 1 December 2026 and duties on Chinese BEVs apply, which management says could lift European volumes, but the impact is not quantified.

rows.label: Maxwell double-digit EBITDA margin
rows.why: Maxwell revenue reached ₹85 crore in Q2 (+94% YoY) and PAT has been positive for consecutive quarters, with management targeting double-digit EBITDA margin in FY28.

tone.note: Management was confident on order flow, EV and non-auto diversification, and the Q3 margin recovery, but cautious on battery pack margins and non-auto targets, and analysts pushed on price pass-through and the timing of the proprietary 4W ramp.

540173|2026-03.headline: PNB Housing Q4 FY26 disbursements rose 36% YoY to INR 9,355 crores; FY27 guidance is loan book above INR 1 lakh crore and ROA 2.4-2.5%.
540173|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 disbursements grew 36% YoY and 50% QoQ to INR 9,355 crores, with retail disbursements up 32% YoY to INR 9,020 crores. PAT rose 19% YoY to INR 656 crores in Q4 and 18% to INR 2,291 crores for FY26, helped by negative credit cost of 45 bps from write-off pool recoveries. Spread compressed 10 bps QoQ to 2.12% on lower incremental yields and balance transfer pressure in Prime, while reported NIM rose 6 bps to 3.69%. Management guided that yields have bottomed out, with FY27 retail loan growth of 18-20%, NIM of 3.55-3.65% and ROA of 2.4-2.5%.

financial_highlights.change: -15 bps QoQ; FY26 7.57% vs 7.86% in FY25
+13% YoY; opex to ATA 1.05% FY26, 1.08% Q4

segments.commentary: Q4 disbursement INR 1,249 crores, up 59% QoQ but flat YoY; FY26 disbursement about INR 3,800 crores, targeted to grow about 50%. Management says GNPA in affordable is below 0.6%.

segments.name: Emerging Market
segments.commentary: Disbursement grew 34% YoY in Q4. Segment share of retail loan book rose with affordable plus emerging at 40% of retail book (37% a year earlier).

segments.name: Prime
segments.commentary: Disbursement grew 43% YoY in Q4 despite yield pressure from rate cuts. Management says Prime disbursement largely replenishes runoff; Prime loan growth is about 9%.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Restarted with INR 335 crores disbursed in Q4 FY26; corporate loan book INR 401 crores at 31 March 2026. Target yield 11.5-12%, capped at about 3% of book in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Loan book to cross INR 1 lakh crore in FY27.
Retail loan book growth of 18-20% in FY27; overall book growth stated as 18-20%.
NIM guided at 3.55-3.65% for FY27; management expects spread-NIM gap to normalise from Q1 FY27.
ROA guided at 2.4-2.5% for FY27.
Credit cost expected to stay negative at about 15-20 bps in FY27, with recoveries of INR 200-250 crores.
Opex to ATA expected to stay in a 1-1.1% range; cost of borrowing stable or 5-10 bps better.
Affordable and emerging to reach about 50% of the book in two to three years; corporate to reach 5-6% in year two and 8-9% in year three.
capex_capacity: Opened 35 branches in Q4 FY26, taking the network to 393 branches (229 affordable, 87 emerging market).
Management said the priority is to make existing branches more productive rather than adding many more.
Infinity in-house digital onboarding app is fully adopted by the in-house sales team; direct selling agents are being onboarded.
Digital channels generate about 15% of leads.
Micro LAP and micro housing products planned for launch in Q1 FY27 in the 14-16% yield segment.
demand_pricing: Management cited intense pricing competition, especially in Q4, and said affordable yield fell about 75 bps QoQ to as low as 11.35%.
