Industry housing finance growth cited at 12-13%; the company describes itself as third-largest in the industry.
Incremental cost of borrowing rose to 7.23% in Q4 from 7.2% in Q3 amid current liquidity conditions.
Non-housing share of the book at 32.4% vs 30.6% in Q3; PBC retail home loans at 65%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the spread fall while NIM rose, and will the ROA gap normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinay Gupta said the divergence is a methodology difference (daily spread convention vs monthly NIM averaging) and should normalise from next quarter, with NIM in a 5-10 bps range of current trajectory.

qa_highlights.question: What credit cost is built into the 2.4-2.5% ROA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinay Gupta said credit cost is expected to remain negative at about 15-20 bps in FY27, with write-off pool recoveries continuing; mix shift to emerging, affordable and corporate should support NIM over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did affordable disbursements weaken and is it linked to asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajai Kumar Shukla said affordable disbursements rebounded in Q4, mid-year challenges were temporary and fixed, and quality is not the reason; Prime disbursement reflects replenishment of runoff.

qa_highlights.question: What early bounce and stress indicators are visible for April?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said April bounce rates are similar to March, with no significant jump; a one-off government-employee EMI bounce was cleared the next day.

qa_highlights.question: Why is management confident yields have bottomed out?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajai Kumar Shukla said no repo change in recent months, so balance transfer outflows should restrict, supporting yield; BT out improved from Q3 to Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What was the nature of the INR 335 crore corporate disbursement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the one case in FY26 was about INR 360-370 crores, primarily in Mumbai; focus is on reputed builders in about seven or eight top cities, with corporate at about 3% of book in FY27.

risks_watch: Yield recovery depends on balance transfer outflows staying restricted and on no further rate cuts; management also flagged possible upside in market rates.
Credit cost is negative because of write-off pool recoveries (about INR 500 crores corporate and INR 325 crores retail remaining); normalisation could weigh on ROA.
Opex grew 13% and the full cost of 35 Q4 branches will flow into FY27; opex to ATA target 1-1.1%.
Cost of borrowing: management expects only stable to 5-10 bps improvement; a rating upgrade is being pursued as a lever.
Geopolitical and crude-oil risk could affect inflation, rates and asset quality, though management sees no early stress as of mid-April.
Prime 30+ DPD on a like-for-like basis is 2.72% (investor presentation figure of 3.31% includes Stage-2 SICR accounts).

rows.label: Cost of borrowing 5-10 bps better, rating upgrade pursued
rows.why: Cost of borrowing is 7.35% in Q4 (FY26 7.57% vs 7.86% FY25), management guides only stable to 5-10 bps better and says a rating upgrade is a lever; incremental cost rose to 7.23% from 7.2%.

rows.label: Yield bottoming on restricted balance transfer outflows
rows.why: BT out fell to 8.6% in Q4 from 8.95% in Q3 with no repo change recently, but intense affordable pricing competition (affordable yield 11.35%) and rate-cut risk remain.

tone.note: Management was confident on disbursement recovery, asset quality (GNPA 0.93%) and yield bottoming, but cautious on cost of borrowing and hedged on geopolitical risk; analysts probed the Q4 spread-NIM divergence, the Prime 30+ DPD figures and the sustainability of negative credit cost.

540173|2026-06.headline: PNB Housing Q1 FY27 PAT rose 4% YoY to INR 557 crore, with ROA 2.37% and ROE 11.44%, while NIM fell 19 bps QoQ to 3.50%.
540173|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 PAT grew 4% YoY to INR 557 crore, with ROA of 2.37% and ROE of 11.44%. Disbursements moved to a cheque-realisation basis this quarter, so reported disbursement grew 18% YoY to INR 5,882 crore against 56% on the old cheque-handover basis. Loan book grew 15% YoY to INR 89,670 crore, NIM moderated to 3.50% and gross NPA was 0.95%. Management says margin and yield have bottomed and expects Q2 to be much better than Q1, especially in Affordable.

financial_highlights.change: -19 bps QoQ (12 bps leverage, 7 bps Q4 true-up)

financial_highlights.metric: Spread / portfolio yield / cost of borrowing
financial_highlights.change: Spread stable QoQ; yield +1 bp; cost of borrowing +1 bp

financial_highlights.value: Negative 12 bps (recoveries INR 67 crore from written-off pool)

segments.name: Prime
segments.commentary: Disbursement INR 3,083 crore in Q1 FY27, double-digit YoY growth; Prime yield up about 8 bps QoQ, which management attributes mostly to mix shift toward self-employed and non-home loans.

segments.name: Emerging Markets
segments.commentary: Disbursement INR 2,029 crore in Q1 FY27, double-digit YoY growth; INR 71 crore disbursed under the new Emerging Developer Finance programme.

segments.name: Affordable / Emerging (retail)
segments.commentary: Affordable and Emerging book grew 27% YoY and is 41% of retail portfolio (target 45% by FY27-end). Affordable net disbursement only INR 555 crore, below target; management cites about 11% YoY growth on a like-for-like basis.

segments.name: Corporate loan book
segments.commentary: INR 493 crore outstanding at 30 June 2026, with about INR 215 crore disbursed in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Written-off pool (retail)
segments.commentary: About INR 340 crore remaining; INR 67 crore recovered in Q1. One legacy account of about INR 420 crore was classified as fraud, already fully provided in FY23, so no incremental P&L impact.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 overall loan book growth guidance of 18% to 20% maintained; management says it expects to beat it.
Affordable loan book growth guidance of 50% to 60% maintained for FY27.
Construction finance capped at about 3% of the overall book in FY27.
Affordable and Emerging share to reach 45% of book by FY27-end and about 50% in FY28.
FY27 ROA guided around 2.4%; FY28 ROA around 2.3% as credit cost normalises. Long-term ROA 2.3% to 2.35%.
NIM expected to have bottomed; gradual improvement from H2 FY27. Yield expected to keep improving on mix.
Credit cost expected to stay negative through FY27 on continued recoveries.
Q2 FY27 disbursement (net) expected 60% to 70% above Q1 overall and 2.5x to 2.6x in Affordable; management says July was promising.
Rating upgrades (CARE done; ICRA and CRISIL pending) expected to cut cost of borrowing by at least about 10 bps.
capex_capacity: Branch network expanded by 12 in the quarter to 404 branches.
Affordable business launched from selected Prime and Emerging branches; about INR 30 crore disbursed in June, and 15% to 18% of Affordable business in July.
Management does not plan to open more branches; plans to use existing branches to contain opex.
Micro-housing policy formulated and rolled out in Q2 FY27; meaningful contribution expected from H2 FY27.
Full buyout transactions started; loan assets of INR 146 crore acquired in Q1 FY27.
demand_pricing: Management cites steady housing demand across retail mortgage segments, particularly Affordable and Emerging Markets; RBI repo unchanged at 5.25%.
Gross disbursement YoY growth of 56% on cheque-handover basis vs 18% on the new net basis; the gap reflects the accounting change, not lost demand.
Incremental disbursement yield is above the 9.48% book yield, per management.
Incremental cost of borrowing rose about 18 bps in Q1 on tighter liquidity and market volatility; management says it has eased somewhat but remains elevated.
BT-in share of sourcing fell to 4.4% from 5% a year ago; Affordable BT-in fell to 3.4% from 10.5%.
Prime yield mix benefit about 10 to 15 bps; Affordable yield up about 50 bps QoQ per management.

qa_highlights.question: How should yield and cost of funds trend, and does the medium-term NIM expansion thesis from mix shift toward Affordable/Emerging/CF still hold over two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin, yield and cost of funds have all bottomed; gradual margin improvement expected from H2 FY27. Construction finance capped at 3% of book in FY27; Affordable and Emerging share at 41% now, targeting 45% by FY27-end and nearly 50% in two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the gross disbursement momentum (55%+ on cheque-handover basis) carry into Q2 and make the 18-20% loan growth guidance conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to beat both gross and net Q2 numbers, said Q2 gross will be much better than Q1 and July showed strong gross and net momentum. It said it expects to do much better than the 18-20% loan growth guidance but did not raise it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did leverage and NII move sharply when debt-to-equity barely changed?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said average leverage rose from 3.6x to 3.75x; Q4 disbursement realisations flowed into Q1 borrowings, and lower investment yields also weighed on total yield.

qa_highlights.question: Is the gap between reported and gross disbursement across all segments, and what is Affordable growth on a like-for-like basis?
qa_highlights.answer: The gap spans Prime, Emerging and Affordable since retail and wholesale moved to debit-from-account recognition. Like-for-like Affordable YoY growth is about 11%.

qa_highlights.question: Will credit cost turn positive in H2, and what ROA path follows?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said credit cost should stay negative through FY27 given line of sight on recoveries. FY27 ROA guided around 2.4%; FY28 around 2.3% as credit cost normalises; long-term 2.3% to 2.35%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did recoveries of about INR 77 crore not fully flow through ECL writeback, and where did the difference go?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said regular OTS settlements cost about INR 10-12 crore, booked as write-offs in Prime and Emerging legacy pool, explaining the gap versus the INR 67 crore recovery figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is Q2 net disbursement growth versus Q1 net, and what does July look like?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall Q2 net disbursement expected about 60-70% above Q1 net; Affordable 2.5x-2.6x Q1 net. Management said July was promising, with Prime and Emerging contributing 15-18% of Affordable business in July.

qa_highlights.question: How much benefit from rating upgrades and when will it show in cost of borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: CARE upgrade is done; ICRA and CRISIL pending. CFO said at least about 10 bps reduction in cost of borrowing should come through; some fresh borrowing already at better rates.

qa_highlights.question: Prime yield rose 8 bps: how much is mix versus like-for-like, and does self-employed mix raise risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed about 10-15 bps benefit to mix shift toward self-employed and non-home loans; without mix, Prime yield would have been roughly stable at 8.92-8.95%. Delinquency in Prime and Emerging said to have improved QoQ.

risks_watch: Affordable execution: Q1 net disbursement of INR 555 crore is below target; Q2 needs 2.5-2.6x Q1 net and 50-60% full-year Affordable growth is guided, with new CBO leadership still unproven.

Credit cost: negative 12 bps in Q1 relies on written-off pool recoveries (INR 67 crore) that will shrink from about INR 340 crore; sustainability of negative credit cost beyond FY27 is open.
Fraud account of about INR 420 crore: fully provided in FY23, but recovery timing and quantum not guided; management declined to quantify expected FY27 recoveries.
Disbursement realisation under cheque-realisation accounting: management expects the transition to flow through over about two months, so Q2 reported figures depend on timing of realisations.
key_quotes: Yes, I think if I talk about Q2, I think we will try to beat both the numbers, which is gross or net.
So I think 18 to 20%, that's the guidance which we are going to definitely, our team is focusing on better growth than what we have given guidance.
Going forward, we feel NIM has largely bottomed out and should start improving from second half of this financial year.
So it was an artificial lift in NIM in Q4, whereas that start getting normalized from Q1 onwards.

540173|2026-09.headline: PNB Housing Q2 FY27 disbursements rose 60% YoY to INR 9,609 crore and spread widened to 2.43%, aided by a one-off; loan book up 19% YoY to INR 95,079 crore.
540173|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was a strong quarter: disbursements of INR 9,609 crore (+60% YoY, including INR 838 crore pool buyout) and retail disbursements at an all-time high of INR 9,250 crore (+54%). Profit after tax rose 6% YoY to INR 617 crore, with ROA of 2.53% and ROE of 12.33%, both flattered by a one-off prepayment recovery; management says normalised ROA is about 2.4%. GNPA improved to 0.91% from 0.95% in Q1, and a INR 75 crore write-off recovery produced negative credit cost of 19 bps. The company was upgraded to AAA by CRISIL, taking all four domestic agencies to AAA, and management expects a phased benefit to borrowing costs.

financial_highlights.change: +60% YoY, includes INR 838 crore pool buyout
+20% YoY from INR 217 crore; opex to ATA 1.03%
includes INR 75 crore write-off recovery; about 11 bps excluding it

financial_highlights.metric: Net worth / book value per share

segments.name: Affordable (Roshni)
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR 1,149 crore, +40% YoY; affordable book up 45% YoY. Management says Roshni yield is flat while prime/emerging-sourced affordable business dilutes overall yield by 10-12 bps.

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR 2,882 crore, +36% YoY; book up 22% YoY. Affordable plus emerging together are 41% of retail book, targeted at 45% by end-FY27.

segments.name: Prime
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR 4,380 crore, +44% YoY. Prime disbursement mix in Q2 was about 60% self-employed and 40% salaried.

segments.name: Corporate

Normalised ROA guidance of about 2.4% maintained.
Credit cost expected to settle at about 10-12 bps once recoveries stop.
FY28 strategy being prepared in Q3; intent is not to degrow. Target of INR 3,000 crore construction finance book this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-off charge from the legacy corporate account and how is it accounted for?
qa_highlights.answer: Overdue charges and overdue interest collected on closure of one legacy corporate account. Accounted for on receipt basis, so booked in Q2 as a one-off; it lifted yield, spread and NIM by roughly 12-17 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sensitivity of cost of borrowing and margins to a 50 bps repo hike?
qa_highlights.answer: A 25 bps hike adds 9-10 bps to cost of borrowing, rising to 12-15 bps by end-Q4; a 50 bps hike would add about 20 bps, with 20-30 bps passed on to the portfolio.

qa_highlights.question: Is rate-hike-driven demand softening, and how are competitors pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: No change in momentum observed so far. Most HFCs have raised rates by 15-20 bps; pass-through expected at 15-20 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: About 11 bps excluding the INR 75 crore recovery; management expects 10-12 bps once recoveries stop.

qa_highlights.question: Why are non-housing loans rising in the mix and how long will this continue?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60% of incremental disbursements (excluding pool buyout) are housing and about 40-48% non-housing, managed within PBC norms; pool sell-down of non-housing assets is being explored.

qa_highlights.question: Why is 30+ DPD on the 24-month vintage up from about 0.2% to 0.4%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not significant, 90+ DPD is stable and bounce rates have improved; the company will deep-dive the trend.

risks_watch: Rate pass-through: borrowing costs are rising with the repo hike, and pass-through may fall short of the 15-20 bps assumed.
Asset quality in affordable LAP and the 30+ DPD trend on newer vintages (0.2% to 0.4% QoQ).
Corporate written-off pool of about INR 650 crore from two accounts declared fraud, still under recovery; retail written-off pool about INR 320 crore.

540180|2026-03.headline: Varun Beverages Q1 CY2026 revenue rose 18.1% to Rs 65,742 mn and EBITDA 21% to Rs 15,289 mn on 16.3% volume growth.
540180|2026-03.overview: Consolidated volumes grew 16.3% to 363.4 mn cases, with India up 14.4% and international up 21.4%, after a weak prior-year summer hit by rains. Consolidated realisation per case rose 1.6% on favourable currency in international markets, while India realisation fell 1.5% on pack upsizing and selective Rs 10 price points. EBITDA margin expanded 55 bps to 23.3% and PAT rose 20.1% to Rs 8,787 mn, though depreciation (+30.9%) and finance cost (+18%) rose on new plants and the Twizza acquisition. Management said it is covered on packaging and raw materials for the current quarter and holds about 6 months of inventory internationally, with the crude-linked cost risk flagged for later quarters.

segments.name: India

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Volume up 21.4%, with management saying all international markets grew double digits except Morocco; Twizza (South Africa) acquired via BevCo at EV ZAR 2,053 mn.

segments.name: Product mix

segments.name: Snacks / food distribution (Africa)
segments.commentary: Q1 snack foods revenue Rs 112 cr vs Rs 52 cr in Q1 CY25; Zimbabwe plant commissioned end of last year.

Four plants commissioned last year (Buxar, Prayagraj, Damtal, Meghalaya) have stabilised; management says it is no longer opening smaller plants and cost of production in larger plants is about half that of smaller ones.
Twizza revenue about Rs 800 cr (last full year), acquisition price about Rs 1,140 cr; Crickley Dairy revenue about Rs 160 cr; combined about Rs 1,000 cr. Margins not yet guided.

Rs 10 price point used selectively, under 2% of total volume, to retain distributors.
Competitors (B-brands, water players) have cut discounts rather than raise prices, per management; PET and can shortages affecting the whole industry.
Ad-Rush (Rs 60 mid-priced energy drink) performing well above plan; can shortage constraining supply. Sting Classic launched in cans and PET (April), with early response described as strong.

qa_highlights.question: What is the near-term impact of higher oil prices on packaging and other costs?
qa_highlights.answer: International raw materials impact practically zero to a couple of points given about 6 months inventory; India has minor impact for this quarter and some for next, offset by lower discounts and cost cuts. Transport cost cannot be stocked but is absorbable.

qa_highlights.question: Why did India realisation improve to -1.5% from -4% last quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Premiumisation through new launches and dairy growth of about 60% (realisation near 3x normal) helped, along with lower discounting and efficiency; Rs 10 price points are used selectively.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company placed on aluminium cans and PET supply?
qa_highlights.answer: Cans are under 2% of sales and tied up above that requirement; shortage is industry-wide and customers may switch to PET or glass.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2-year CAGR slowdown in India a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the 6-8% figure, citing a 23% average CAGR historically; said last year was an exceptional weather-hit year and growth should stay double-digit.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a margin hit if crude stays high for several quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it holds 6 months inventory and expects competitors to take price increases or absorb the hit first; does not expect to take a hit itself.

qa_highlights.question: Is the upsizing from 250 ml to 400 ml adding consumption, and is India margin affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Consumption is rising both in litres and in units; full-quarter upsizing effects already absorbed by volumes and plant efficiency, with minor upsides to be absorbed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plant payback and utilisation impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Normal payback 3-4 years at around 30% RoCE; higher utilisation is helping as larger lines (1,000 bottles per minute vs 200) replace old high-cost plants.

540180|2026-06.headline: VBL Q2 CY2026 revenue rose 20.4% to Rs 84,512.3 mn and EBITDA 17.2% to Rs 23,430.4 mn, with India volume up 14.4%.
540180|2026-06.overview: Consolidated sales volume grew 19.8% to 466.7 million cases in the quarter, with net revenue up 20.4% year-on-year. India volume grew 14.4%, with growth of about 20% or more in every month since March except April, which was roughly flat due to El Nino-driven rain. International volumes rose 38.4%, including 11.8 million cases from the newly consolidated Twizza business in South Africa. EBITDA margin fell 76 bps to 27.7% on Twizza's lower margins, while India margin improved 38 bps. Management also extended the PepsiCo bottling licence to April 2049 and announced the Calpis tie-up with Asahi and the Devyani Kenya acquisition.

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue from operations (net of excise and GST)

financial_highlights.value: Rs 0.50 per share (25% of face value), cash outflow ~Rs 1,691 million

segments.name: India

India EBITDA margin improved 38 bps on operating efficiencies, partly offset by higher transport and distribution costs. Low-sugar/no-sugar products were about 73% of consolidated volume in H1.

segments.commentary: Volume rose 38.4% including 11.8 million cases from Twizza in South Africa; ex-Twizza growth was above 25%. Management said all African markets are growing except Zambia, which is small and slower. Twizza operates at lower margins, which diluted group EBITDA margin.

segments.commentary: Management said VAD is growing above 40% and Nimbooz above 30% for the company, about 3x-4x the overall business. Growth figures were given only as ranges, with no absolute values.

segments.commentary: Management said this business is growing about 50%. No absolute figures or targets were given.

Management said India can keep growing in double digits despite a stronger competitive field from Campa and Coca-Cola, and argued the industry is growing about 20%.

Raw material costs have risen with the West Asia crisis. Part of the increase is booked in Q2 under average costing, and the balance will hit Q3. Management said the impact will not be large and pricing will hold.
Management said EBITDA margins can be maintained even in a high-crude year and would improve once the conflicts ease.
Energy drink labels must drop the word 'energy' within 90 days, per the regulator's guidance. Management said volumes are returning to STING as new labels roll out.
Management will not scale Rs 10 pricing for now, as it is not profitable for the company, unless monthly growth falls below 20%.

Capital work-in-progress of ~Rs 4,900 mn at 30 June 2026, mainly South Africa expansion and a CSD line in Kenya.

Pack changes: the company is upsizing and downsizing packs by market. Management said volume is reported on an 8-ounce basis, and realisation per 8-ounce case and gross margin are said to be stable.

Management declined to give market share data, saying it does not track share.

qa_highlights.question: Is there room to scale the Rs 10 price point, and how much of the April weakness was rain versus competition from Campa?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not scaling Rs 10 because it is unprofitable. It said India is growing 20%+ month-on-month outside April, which was hit by El Nino.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company expanding into alcobev in India, and is it bidding for Bira?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is only looking at possible new categories and is not bidding for Bira. Prathmesh Mishra was hired for the group, not the company.

qa_highlights.question: Can India grow at low double digits given stronger competitors and a high base?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman Ravi Jaipuria said H1 India growth was 14.4% and July is continuing at the same trend, so double-digit growth looks achievable. Varun Jaipuria said weather, not demand, was holding back growth in months without rain.

qa_highlights.question: Up to what crude level can margins be maintained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are maintainable even in a worse geopolitical year and that margins cannot get worse once conflicts ease. It did not give a crude threshold.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the energy drink labelling change on STING?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said June and July saw a temporary dip as volume moved to CSD. Volumes are returning as new labels roll out, and the regulator gave 90 days to remove the word 'energy'.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Calpis tie-up extend to other Asahi brands or other categories?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current focus is stabilising Calpis. Dairy is a core category, and no decision has been made on RTD tea or coffee.

Lower Twizza margins, which pulled group EBITDA margin down 76 bps; further integration and dilution is possible.
Energy drink labelling change, with a 90-day compliance deadline. Some volume shifted to CSD in June-July.
Rising competitive intensity from Campa Cola's Rs 10 and Rs 20 packs and Coca-Cola, which could pressure India volume and pricing.
Net debt of ~Rs 3,730 mn at consolidated level after the Twizza acquisition.

540180|2026-09.headline: VBL Q3 CY2026 revenue rose 33.2% to Rs 66,076 mn, with gross margin down 334 bps to 53.1% on packaging cost inflation.
540180|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 33.2% YoY to Rs 66,076 mn and EBITDA rose 25.1% to Rs 14,267 mn, with EBITDA margin at 21.6% (down 140 bps). Volume growth was 28.7% consolidated, with India at 22.5% and international at 39.9%. Gross margin fell 334 bps to 53.1% as packaging inflation from the geopolitical conflict (around 300 bps) and a surge in lower-margin preform and cap sales (about 100 bps in India) weighed. Management said gross margin has likely troughed at current prices, and it announced an interim dividend of Rs 0.50 per share and a KIVA Spirits entry into alcobev/RTD.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Volume grew 22.5% in Q3; realisation per case rose 0.5%. EBITDA margin was broadly stable YoY in 9M CY2026 despite input cost pressure. Low/no-sugar share rose to 88% from 44% a year ago.

segments.name: International (Africa)
segments.commentary: Volume grew 39.9% in Q3, with realisation up on South Africa pricing and FX. International gross margin pressure was about 272 bps versus about 300 bps in India. Twizza merged with BevCo effective 1 Aug 2026.

segments.name: Product mix (volume, Q3)
segments.commentary: CSD 73.3%, juice-based drinks 4.8%, packaged water 21.9% of sales volume. Non-beverage sales (preforms, caps) in India rose about 104%.

guidance_outlook: Management said gross margin has broadly troughed in Q3 CY2026 at current price trends, barring new macro surprises.
Upside to margins could come from price-pack architecture changes, following the Sting pack downsize from 300 ml to 250 ml.
Management said more than half of the 3-4% gross margin impact has been mitigated through cost reductions.
International capex is about USD 90-100 mn; India capex is about Rs 1,000 crore, including a greenfield plant at Suratgarh, Rajasthan and a PET line. CY2026 capex is complete.
Management plans to add about 100,000 outlets a year from the current 4.2 mn, and is aggressively planning numeric and weighted distribution for CY2027.
Calpis launch is planned for December-January, with a broader marketing calendar around late February or March.
capex_capacity: Capacity is full in most African markets; Morocco capacity is short ahead of its season and new lines are planned in Morocco, Zimbabwe and DRC.
South Africa and DRC seasons run November to January with plants at full speed; Twizza gives enough South African capacity this year.
Zimbabwe has a capacity gap that Zambia will partly cover from this month, and more capacity is being added next year.
rPET is about 25% of PET needs via in-house backward integration; the next rPET plant is expected to be operational within 1-2 quarters.
Capex across India and international markets is roughly Rs 1,000 crore and USD 90 mn respectively.
demand_pricing: India volume growth is 22.5%, and 9M India growth is about 16-17%; management said volume growth has been positive since May.
No list-price increase on CSD in Q3; realisation gains came from mix, premium launches (Ad Rush, Evervess mixers), calibrated discounting and price-pack architecture.

Sting pack reduced from 300 ml to 250 ml around May-June to offset raw-material costs. Energy category volumes were hit by an FSSAI labelling ruling; management estimated negativity at about 25% mid-quarter and said Sting is now recovering.
Rs 10 price point is about 0.2-0.3% of volume; management will not push it because unit economics do not work at 150 ml.
Africa: Mondelez exclusive distribution agreement in Zimbabwe (Mondelez has about USD 11 mn existing business there). Kenya beverage operations started with BOLT UP and XTREME FIZZ.
Management said October is still in progress and declined to comment on October trends.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for gross margins next quarter and March quarter, and split of packaging, sugar and non-beverage impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the packaging cost hit applies from purchases after the war began around 28 Feb; the company was covered for one quarter. It said the sugar impact was offset by low/no-sugar mix, and the 3-4% gross margin impact is more than half mitigated.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q3 gross margin the trough?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, broadly, at present price trends, with upside from price-pack changes. The pace of roll-down to other packs will determine that upside.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a sugar or packaging price increase on CSD, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: No CSD price increase was taken in Q3; the only pack change was Sting 300 ml to 250 ml around May-June.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the crude/PET cost increase is in the P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 100% impact of crude is already built in, and rPET (about 25% of PET) has helped contain costs.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new entrant part of the beverage association discussing price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no common forum; industry chatter is about price-pack and trade margin responses if costs stay high.

Energy category recovery after the FSSAI labelling ruling; Sting volumes are recovering but not yet at baseline.

540203|2026-06.headline: Sheela Foam Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 26% to INR1,032 crore and EBITDA 45% to INR109 crore, with margin at 10.6%.
540203|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 26% YoY to INR1,032 crore and EBITDA rose 45% to INR109 crore, with margin up 139 bps to 10.6%. Standalone India revenue grew 20% to INR761 crore and EBITDA 13% to INR68 crore, with gross margin compressed by sharp raw-material (TDI/polyol) swings that management attributes to the Middle East conflict. Management chose to keep growing foam volumes, which was cash-accretive, and international subsidiaries (Australia, Spain) posted sharply higher margins on inventory gains. Management reiterated a 15% EBITDA margin target for next year and expects volumes to recover in the festive quarters.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gains came from longer-held low-cost inventory and yield and supply chain programmes. Overseas momentum should moderate as India recovers, with normal inventory levels by Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone volume growth slow to single digits and margins fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a price-volume trade-off after the steep price hikes, and expects double-digit volume growth for the year once volatility eases. Gross margins were hit mainly by foam, while incremental foam sales generated cash.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 15% EBITDA margin target and 13-14% FY28 guidance hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not guided for 13% for FY27 (only 11-12%) but stands by its margin commitment; the current volatility makes it hard to comment, and gross margin has fallen more than the guided range.

qa_highlights.answer: Furlenco is present in 40-50 shop-in-shop stores with a first target of 100, and will go only where it fits its micro-market strategy.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup and outlook of other income (INR22 crore over past two quarters)?

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for the INR5,000 crore revenue and INR600 crore EBITDA target?

qa_highlights.question: Will the 13-15% EBITDA margin target for next year still be met?

qa_highlights.question: Will volumes be reported by channel for the Sleepwell brand?

qa_highlights.question: How much did the Australian provision impact results?

qa_highlights.question: Mattress volume outlook for H2 FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Consolidation accounting and minority interest after Furlenco became a subsidiary?

qa_highlights.question: Debt outlook for FY27 and FY28?

540205|2026-03.headline: Aditya Vision Q4 FY26 revenue rose 28% YoY to INR625 crore and PAT 36% to INR22 crore, despite a weak summer and FY26 PAT up only 11%.

segments.name: Jharkhand
segments.commentary: 12% of both Q4 and FY26 revenue; 33 stores covering 22 of 24 districts.

segments.name: Chhattisgarh
segments.commentary: Entered early with 3 stores covering 2 of 33 districts; no revenue split disclosed.

Management expects opex to grow in line with overall expenses rather than rise faster, as the store base becomes more mature.

Price increases on mobiles and laptops lowered the margin mix; management said price hikes are not the main driver of profitability.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 50% rise in other expenses?

qa_highlights.question: What are the normalised margins for mature Bihar, and when will UP match them?

qa_highlights.question: What is the store expansion target for FY27 and FY28?

qa_highlights.question: When will EBITDA margin return to about 9%?

Opex rising faster than revenue in new geographies (UP, Chhattisgarh, MP) could weigh on EBITDA margins.

540205|2026-09.headline: Aditya Vision Q2 FY27 revenue rose 28.1% YoY to Rs 586.23 crore and PAT 45.2% to Rs 18.47 crore, with October demand described as slow.
540205|2026-09.overview: Revenue, EBITDA and PAT all grew strongly in Q2 FY27, with H1 revenue up 27.3% to Rs 1,778.91 crore and same-store sales growth at 18%. Gross margin expanded 125 bps to 16.3%, but management attributed only about 75-80 bps of the quarter's margin gain to price hikes and guided normalised gross margin at 15-15.5%. Management said demand has been slow in October and expects a pick-up toward Dhanteras and Diwali. The store network reached 214, with new entries into Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and West Bengal, and the company guided to about 230-235 stores by FY27 end.

segments.commentary: Contributed about 73% of Q2 revenue across all 38 districts, with 120 stores.

segments.name: Uttar Pradesh
segments.commentary: Contributed about 15% of Q2 revenue from 56 stores across 32 of 75 districts.

segments.name: Jharkhand
segments.commentary: Contributed about 11% of Q2 revenue from 33 stores across 22 of 24 districts.

segments.name: Chhattisgarh
segments.commentary: Contributed about 1% of Q2 revenue from five stores across three of 33 districts; newly entered state.

Store count expected at around 230, possibly up to 235, by end FY27, and about 35 more stores in FY28 (about 270 total).
Chhattisgarh: 9-10 more stores planned. Madhya Pradesh: about 3 stores shortly and 15-17 in the coming year. West Bengal: at least 15 stores, with 40-50 stores possible over about four years.
New-store breakeven expected in about one year; management said new-state margin dilution would be offset by maturing older stores.

Capex in West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh could be 10%-15% higher than in core markets due to freight and vendor logistics costs, depending on store size.
Retail footprint expanded 18.3% to about 9.51 lakh sq ft as of September 30, 2026.
Entered West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh in the period (as of October 2026); two West Bengal stores opened and two more in progress.
Cluster-based expansion leverages logistics, vendor relationships and brand recall.
demand_pricing: Management said demand has been slow in October and expects a pick-up as Dhanteras and Diwali approach.
Q2 growth was led by AC, followed by mobile and refrigerators, helped by an extended summer.
Around 75-80 bps of the Q2 gross margin gain came from OEM price increases; the rest came from normal trading.
H1 same-store sales growth was 18%, versus 2% in H1 FY26 when unseasonal rains hurt footfall.
West Bengal competitors include Reliance and Croma, plus a local chain, which are stronger in metros than in peripheral districts; the company is targeting border districts near Bihar first.
Headwinds cited: West Asia conflict, energy disruption, higher crude prices, Bihar floods and cyclone, and rising staples and cooking gas prices.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 125 bps gross margin expansion in Q2, and is the full-year margin guidance changing?

qa_highlights.question: How has demand been in October and was the festive season delayed?

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and breakeven for new stores in West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about Rs 90 lakh per store, with breakeven expected in about one year; management said it was too early to guide on the new states specifically.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 8th Pay Commission be a demand driver?

540212|2026-03.headline: TCI Express Q4 FY26 revenue rose 6% YoY to INR 327 crore, EBITDA margin 11.3%, PAT flat at INR 21 crore amid fuel and labour cost pressure.
540212|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew about 6% YoY to INR 327 crore and 4% QoQ, with total income of INR 331 crore. EBITDA rose 11% YoY to INR 37 crore (11.3% margin) while PAT was flat at INR 21 crore (6.3% margin). Full-year revenue grew about 2% to INR 1,236 crore, with PAT of INR 90 crore (7.2% margin). Management said the Gulf conflict pushed ATF prices up sharply and labour costs rose, and volume growth slowed to 4% YoY in Q4 after March.

segments.name: Surface Express
segments.commentary: Largest contributor; management said surface margin should improve with diesel-linked price pass-through, citing about 30% arbitrage. Surface grew in single digits in the last two quarters, with mid-single-digit to ~10% growth expected going forward.

segments.name: Multimodal (Air, Rail, C2C, e-commerce)
segments.commentary: About 18.5% of FY26 revenue, with management citing about 20% growth; target of 22% to 25% share over 2 to 3 years. Domestic and international air margins were hit this quarter, while rail and C2C margins were described as stable.

segments.name: Rail Express
segments.commentary: Management said rail gross profit is above 30% and realisation is about 2.5x surface. Rail volumes are not disclosed.

segments.name: E-commerce Express
segments.commentary: About 2.5% of business, with a target of 5%. Focus is on D2C and B2B merchant-to-warehouse movement with SME clients, not quick commerce.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guided at about 10% to 11%, with revenue growth of about 15% including price hikes.
FY27 margin improvement of 100 to 150 basis points at EBITDA and PAT levels, conditional on fuel prices stabilising.
Q1 FY27 volume expected at high single-digit growth, improving QoQ through the year.
Multimodal growth guided at about 20% in FY27.
Depreciation run-rate of INR 30 to 32 crore per year after ROU additions; about INR 6 to 6.25 crore per quarter.
Capex plan revised from INR 500 crore to INR 400 crore for FY23 to FY27; about INR 130 crore planned for FY27. A new five-year plan will follow.
Branch expansion of about 100 branches in FY27 (40 surface, 60 rail, air and C2C).
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation was about 83.25% in Q4, improved QoQ.
Nagpur sorting centre upgraded and now owned; semi-automated, about 70,000 to 75,000 sq ft, with only 5% to 7% change in cut-off time.
Ahmedabad and Kolkata sorting centres under construction, to finish in FY27, with automation ramping up in the first half of FY28. Lucknow also in progress.
Mumbai and Kolkata sorting centres moved to 5-year leases, which added ROU assets and raised depreciation.
Next sorting centres planned for Chennai and Bangalore.
demand_pricing: Management said diesel rose about INR 8 and the company is passing it on to customers, with 85% pass-through expected and 10% to 15% of customers still negotiating.
Air fuel (ATF) rose about 50% and international air rates went up 2x to 3x after the Gulf conflict began at end-February, leading customers to hold shipments in March.
Labour costs rose 15% to 20%, adding about 100 basis points to overall cost, per management.
SME share of revenue was 48% to 52% against a historical 50:50 split; management expects a return to 50%+ with the last two months' results described as good.
Revenue per kg is about INR 12.3 to 12.4 with EBITDA of about INR 1.25 to 1.27 per kg, against a historical INR 1.8 to 2.0 per kg, per an analyst's calculation.
The company expects to benefit from air-to-surface and rail shifts as higher air prices push customers to other modes.

qa_highlights.question: Why has growth been restricted and margins fallen from 15% to 16% to 10% to 11%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the Gulf war and ATF spike, airline consolidation, airport privatisation, lower truck utilisation and a 100 bps hit from labour costs. It guided FY27 PAT margin recovery of 100 to 150 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume and revenue guidance?

qa_highlights.answer: Management said air margins were temporarily hit by costs. Rail and C2C margins are stable and surface margin should improve with diesel pass-through.

Rupee weakness raising input costs.
SME stress and the share of SME revenue, which fell to 48% to 52%.

540212|2026-06.headline: TCI Express Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to INR 312 crore, with PAT up 6% to INR 22.4 crore and volumes up 7.5% to 2.5 lakh tonnes.
540212|2026-06.overview: Income from operations grew about 9% YoY to INR 312 crore and EBITDA rose 11% to INR 37 crore, with margin at 11.7% versus 11.5%. PAT rose 6% to INR 22.4 crore (7.1% margin). Management said the fuel price hike taken in mid-May was only partly reflected in Q1 (June only), so benefits should show from Q2. The company stated it is debt-free with net cash of about INR 118 crore.

financial_highlights.change: up ~6% YoY from INR 21 crore; margin 7.1%

segments.name: Surface Express
segments.commentary: Largest contributor; grew 9% YoY on existing customers, new accounts and industrial growth. Management targets accelerating to double-digit growth.

segments.name: Domestic Air Express
segments.commentary: Grew 29% YoY per opening remarks (CEO-level figure); later cited ~28% on enterprise account wins and airline partnerships.

segments.name: International Express
segments.commentary: Grew 27% YoY on new customers, win-backs and expanded global carrier partnerships.

segments.name: E-commerce Express
segments.commentary: Grew 63% YoY, the fastest-growing vertical, but only ~2-2.5% of revenue; target small-merchant, D2C and e-commerce B2B segments at 16-18% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Rail Express / C2C Express
segments.commentary: Rail added operational branches; C2C added clients, regional branch coverage and a larger dedicated vehicle fleet. No growth figures disclosed.

FY27 PAT growth guided at 20-25%.

SME to B2B mix returned to 50:50 in Q1 from 48:52 in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What were the Q1 volumes and price hikes versus peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume was 2.5 lakh tonnes, up ~7.5%. Management said fuel-linked pass-through came in mid-May, with the full price increase reflected mainly in June; the company deferred hikes ahead of expected fuel increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the strategic rationale for expanding e-commerce given lower margins historically?
qa_highlights.answer: E-commerce is ~2-2.5% of revenue. Management said D2C margins are 16-18% and it is targeting small merchants, D2C and e-commerce B2B, with regional teams and branches to support Surface.

qa_highlights.question: What changed to drive consistent double-digit EBITDA growth and volume acceleration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it strengthened vertical-wise regional teams and built regional structures across Air, International, Rail and C2C. Air grew ~28% on new customers, and a clear pipeline supports growth.

qa_highlights.question: What are the volume, pricing and PAT targets for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth of 11-12%, net price hikes of about 3%, total growth of 13-15%, and PAT growth of 20-25%.

540212|2026-09.headline: TCI Express Q2 FY27 EBITDA rose 10.8% YoY to INR 43 crore with margin at 12.7%, guiding 14-15% growth and 13%+ margin for H2.
540212|2026-09.overview: Standalone income from operations grew about 9% YoY to INR 336 crore in Q2 FY27, with EBITDA up around 11% to INR 43 crore and margin expanding to 12.7% from 12.4%, the highest in five quarters. PAT rose 6% to INR 27 crore and H1 PAT rose 6% to INR 49 crore. Management said volumes were 265,000 tonnes, up 7.5% YoY, and that October was strong. The call focused on the growth of E-Commerce Express and air/rail services, capex for sorting centres, and competitive pressure from aggregators, which management said is not affecting B2B pricing.

financial_highlights.change: up ~11% YoY from INR 39 crore; up 16% QoQ
from 12.4% a year ago; highest in five quarters
up 10.8% from INR 72 crore; margin from 12%
liquid assets INR 93 crore vs total debt INR 15 crore (temporary)

segments.name: Surface Express
segments.commentary: Largest business, grew around 9%+ YoY in Q2 and H1. Management said it expects total growth of 14-15% in H2 with volume growth of 11-12%.

segments.name: Domestic Air Express
segments.commentary: Grew about 29% YoY; management is building a separate air network covering about 20 cities.

segments.commentary: Grew about 26% YoY.

segments.commentary: Grew about 52% YoY (company said 51.6%). Management describes it as a small business and is focusing on D2C, small e-commerce players and Tier 2 cities; target EBITDA margin of 15%.

segments.commentary: Declined YoY because fuel-price volatility made rates unattractive; management expects growth to resume from Q3.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 revenue growth guided at 14-15%, with volume growth around 11-12%.
H2 FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 13%+; management expects margin expansion of at least 50-100 bps for FY27 over FY26.
Price increases net around 1.5% after passing through fuel costs; management expects price hikes to continue in Q3 and Q4.
Share of non-Surface services (Air Express, International Air, Rail, E-Commerce, C2C) is about 17-17.5%; target is 18%+ by FY27 year-end and above 22% by 2030.

Capex plan of about INR 100 crore+ per year over the next four to five years, with conversion of 12-15 sorting centres (6-7 done, 3 more by FY27 end), and three major locations (Mumbai, Chennai, Bangalore) over three to four years.
capex_capacity: Tonnage in Q2 was 265,000 tonnes, up 7.5% YoY; capacity utilisation was not quantified.
Current INR 400 crore capex programme (cut from INR 500 crore) is about INR 80 crore spent in H1, with INR 40-50 crore remaining to finish in FY27.
Three new centres (Lucknow, Ahmedabad, Kolkata) to be ready by FY27 year-end; corporate office construction ongoing; automation at Ahmedabad and Kolkata to finish by Q1 or Q2 FY28.
Two automated sorting centres cut labour and truck turnaround time, saving at least 40-50 bps of direct cost per annum, per management.
Management plans to move from leased to owned centres, targeting 80-85% of revenue through owned centres by end-2030 or 2031. Only one centre is promoter-owned.
demand_pricing: Management said pricing is not a talking point in the industry and no one is asking for price cuts; freight is about 1.5% of cargo value.
Management says aggregator and app-based platforms mainly serve B2C, and B2B customers deal directly, so there is no demand impact on Surface Express.

E-Commerce strategy: focus on D2C, merchant connections and small e-commerce players, Tier 2 cities (Surat, Ludhiana, Bengaluru), and profitable business only. SME vs large account split stayed at 50:50.
A digital wallet for e-commerce bookings was signed and is being integrated, with booking expected from next year.
Management said October was strong and the H2 pipeline is robust across all service lines.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of aggregators such as Shiprocket on volumes and on Surface Express?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said aggregators mainly affect B2C; B2B customers contact TCI directly, so there is no impact on Surface Express. TCI also registers with aggregators, but this is a small part of E-Commerce Express.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide to 14-15% growth in H2 and is the pricing premium intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed 14-15% growth and 11-12% volume growth for H2, with net price increases of about 1.5% and no industry price cuts. Non-Surface services are only 1-2 points of the mix, so Surface Express growth is about 9%.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans and returns on converted sorting centres?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it plans about INR 100 crore+ per year, and automated centres have cut direct cost by 40-50 bps. Returns are initially weighing on ROI and expected to improve over 20-25 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did C2C Express decline and what is the H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: C2C declined because fuel-price volatility made rates unattractive; rates have normalised and management expects growth to return from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Indian Railway's own parcel booking services a threat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Railway cannot do door-to-door collection and has only 30-45 minutes to unload at stations, so TCI sees it as a complement to its branch network with 99% service level.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin does E-Commerce Express target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets at least 15% EBITDA margin on D2C accounts and aims to return to 15-16% over two to three years, declining to take business below that.

540222|2026-03.headline: Laurus FY26 revenue rose 23% to INR6,813 crore and EBITDA margin hit 26.8%, with Q4 margin at 28.9%; FY27 capex guided to about INR3,000 crore over two years.
540222|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a strong year: revenue of INR6,813 crore (+23%), gross margin about 60.4%, EBITDA of INR1,826 crore (26.8% margin, +6.7 pp) and PAT of INR889 crore (+148%). Q4 revenue grew only 5% YoY to INR1,812 crore, but Q4 EBITDA margin reached 28.9% on operating leverage and better mix. CDMO grew about 38% in small molecules to INR1,896 crore, while Affordable Medicines (formerly Generics) grew 18% to INR4,733 crore. Management raised its multi-year capex expectation sharply, to around INR3,000 crore over the next two years from the earlier INR1,000 crore a year reference, and the call stressed CDMO share rising to 50% by FY30.

540293|2026-06.headline: Pricol Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 23.5% YoY to Rs 1,083.6 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.41% on West Asia-driven cost headwinds.
540293|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was about Rs 1,083.58 crore, up 23.46% YoY, with EBITDA of Rs 123.69 crore (11.41% margin) and PAT of Rs 67.02 crore (6.19% margin). Management said EBITDA grew only about 21% YoY because of polymer, LPG, freight, rupee and minimum-wage cost increases, which it expects to recover through quarterly and half-yearly indexation over Q2 and Q3. The call also covered a proposed demerger of the DIS/DICVS business from the ACFMS and polymer businesses, a Rs 700 crore capex cycle, and a one-year pause on M&A.

540358|2026-03.headline: RMC Switchgears FY26 consolidated revenue rose 26.4% to Rs 401.59 crore, but profit fell short, with Q4 back to Rs 9.3 crore net profit after a Q3 loss of Rs 7.07 crore.
540358|2026-03.overview: Management framed the call as an analyst day rather than a results discussion, covering FY26 as a year of progress and learning. Consolidated revenue grew 26.4% to Rs 401.59 crore, but margins were hit by PulseBox product development spend, rain-delayed execution in Maharashtra, and solar EPC cost pressure from China-linked supply, safeguard duty and aluminium/silver prices. Q4 returned to profit (Rs 9.3 crore) from a Rs 7.07 crore loss in Q3, which management attributed to execution catch-up and better material availability. Receivables rose from Rs 148 crore to Rs 205 crore and operating cash flow turned negative; management attributed this mainly to March-concentrated billing. No FY27 revenue or profit guidance was given; management said the unexecuted order book is about Rs 850 crore plus and the tender pipeline about Rs 1,500 crore plus.

540366|2026-03.headline: Music Broadcast Q4 FY26 revenue fell to INR 40.8 cr (from INR 54 cr) but operating EBITDA turned positive at INR 6.1 cr (15% margin) on cost cuts.
540366|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue declined to INR 40.8 crore from INR 54 crore a year earlier, as advertiser spend stayed subdued in certain categories. Cost restructuring and hub-based operations lifted operating EBITDA to INR 6.1 crore from negative INR 3.5 crore, with margin at 15%. Reported PAT was a loss of about INR 48 crore (the call also cited an adjusted loss of INR 47.4 crore), versus a loss of INR 38 crore a year earlier. For FY26, revenue fell to INR 174 crore from INR 234 crore, while operating EBITDA margin rose to 18% from 17%, and the reported PAT loss widened to INR 53 crore from INR 33.8 crore.

540376|2026-06.headline: DMart FY26 revenue near INR67,000 crore (+16%), PAT margin ~4.8%; management targets ~15% annual store additions and says SSSG stays at last year's levels.
540376|2026-06.overview: This was DMart's annual analyst call, the first with Anshul Asawa as MD & CEO, covering FY26 results and the outlook for FY27. Management said the fundamentals were intact but flagged higher staff costs for capability build, a slowdown in same-store growth in mature metro stores, and heavy competitive pressure from quick commerce. Avenue E-commerce (DMart Ready) was narrowed to 11 cities after exits from seven cities, with its EBITDA falling about 43% and a net loss of INR307 crore. Management reiterated a roughly 15% internal store-addition target and did not disclose e-commerce KPIs.

qa_highlights.question: Will SSSG recover to double-digit levels given quick-commerce and maturity pressures in metros?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SSSG is likely to hover around the current range (~7-8%) and not rise considerably, especially for older stores; new stores are opened nearby to reduce pressure on existing stores.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the 15% store-addition target conservative and can it go to 100-150 stores a year?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal target is ~15%; capital and people are not constraints, and land acquisition, permissions and build time (2-3 years) are. Management said 100-150 stores is not a reasonable number at about 500 stores currently.

qa_highlights.question: What is the economics of leasing versus owning stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share lease vs owned economics; said both models work. 68 stores are on long leases and 15 of the 85 stores added in FY26 were leased. Niladri said PBT is a fair measure of lease impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the mix of AEL get cut to 11 cities and why not experiment with faster delivery?
qa_highlights.answer: Seven cities were exited because their contribution was minimal. Management said it will not pursue immediate delivery; it will prove the six-hour slotted model in 11 cities first because losses had grown with expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the rise in employee costs and why are contractual headcounts lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Permanent headcount rose ~4,000 (75-80% of additions are store-management cohorts). Frontline staff are non-permanent; productivity and mechanisation held down non-permanent headcount. Wage code from December 2025 also added costs.

qa_highlights.answer: Management does not see a risk of LFL falling below 5%; it sees organised retail still under-penetrated in smaller towns and has no point of view on QC adoption outside top cities.

540401|2026-06.headline: Maximus Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 52% YoY to INR59.91 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 7.64% from 9.81% on Middle East war input costs.
540401|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR59.91 crores versus INR39.52 crores a year earlier, with EBITDA up about 18% to INR4.58 crores. Margin compression, attributed to higher input and freight costs from the ongoing Middle East war, and higher finance costs (INR1.53 crores vs INR0.92 crores) left PAT at INR2.05 crores versus INR2.33 crores a year ago. Management highlighted the proposed associate acquisition of Quebec Petroleum (40% stake), a Kenya grease plant planned for Q3 FY27, and a Tanzania warehousing expansion. Management guided to crossing about INR200 crores revenue in FY27 on a conservative basis.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Highest EBITDA margin among the three verticals (manufacturing, toll blending, trading) in Q1 FY27 and historically. Operations in UAE and Kenya.

segments.name: Toll blending
segments.commentary: Management says it is being pursued aggressively; in talks with an East African MNC for toll blending.

segments.name: Trading
segments.commentary: Lowest-margin vertical per management. Long-term target split: manufacturing plus toll blending 75-80%, trading 20-25%.

segments.name: Specialty lubricants
segments.commentary: Contribute around 40% of topline, per CFO.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue expected to cross about INR200 crores on a conservative basis, with healthy EBITDA margins (stated even under the ongoing war scenario).
Margins expected to hold at current levels or improve over the next couple of quarters if supply disruption persists, through product mix diversification.
Kenya grease manufacturing facility planned for commissioning in Q3 FY27.
Tanzania expansion: initially warehousing and distribution, moving to manufacturing once scale is reached.
Recently launched modernisation programme: automated batch blending, additional storage and warehousing, improved filling lines, and capacity expansion at UAE and Kenya plants.
Capacity considered sufficient for next 2-3 years on single-shift basis; additional storage capex needed for full utilisation.
capex_capacity: Combined manufacturing capacity of about 50,000 KL across UAE and Kenya plants.
Capacity utilisation at about 45% across both units.
Kenya grease plant to cater to East African market, which has few grease manufacturers; also to support toll blending.
Proposed acquisition of an additional manufacturing unit as an associate; process underway, details to be shared later.
Quebec Petroleum: associate investment with initial 40% stake, aimed at entering the Indian domestic market.
demand_pricing: Management says demand for lubricants is supported by industrialisation, infrastructure, vehicle ownership and mining, power and construction; customers are shifting toward premium and specialty products.
Cited Middle East and Africa lubricant market growing from about USD 9.1 billion (2024) to USD 12.4 billion (2034).
Company serves more than 400 customers across 25+ countries and 50+ industries.
Top 10 customers account for roughly 70-75% of revenue, including distributors; company sells mainly through distributors, not B2C.
Product prices and landed costs (freight, insurance) rose due to the Middle East war; company passed on a partial cost increase, which also raised receivables.
Base oil and white oil prices are positively correlated with crude, with a lagged and non-identical impact on lubricant prices.
In Kenya, incumbents Shell and Total have not changed payment terms despite new entrants.

qa_highlights.question: How sensitive are margins to base oil and crude price movements?
qa_highlights.answer: Not directly coupled but positively correlated; raw materials (base oils and white oils) move in the same direction with a lag and not in the same proportion.

qa_highlights.question: Current utilisation of the 50,000 KL capacity, and targets over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: About 45% utilised; capacity is sufficient for 2-3 years on a single shift, but full utilisation would need additional storage capex.

qa_highlights.question: Which vertical has the highest EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Manufacturing, both in Q1 FY27 and historically; toll blending is being pursued more aggressively.

qa_highlights.question: Share of premium and specialty versus conventional revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Specialty lubricants contribute around 40% of topline.

qa_highlights.question: Why have receivables risen faster than revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher topline (about 50% growth), higher product prices and landed costs from the war, and partial pass-through of cost increases to selling prices.

qa_highlights.question: What if supply disruption lasts more than six months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has onboarded new customers and broadened product baskets; margins may dip further but aim to hold or improve through diversification; still expects over INR200 crores revenue in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How will Quebec Petroleum contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Associate with 40% stake; its profits will be included in consolidated financials; focus is India domestic market, while Maximus covers Middle East, East and North Africa.

qa_highlights.question: Target revenue split between trading and toll blending over three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Manufacturing plus toll blending 75-80%, trading 20-25%; split between manufacturing and toll blending not disclosed as they overlap in co-branding.

qa_highlights.question: Concentration of revenue and B2B versus B2C mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Top 10 customers about 70-75% of revenue (distributors included); no own retail outlets; major revenue comes via distribution channels.

risks_watch: Margin compression: EBITDA margin down about 217 bps YoY to 7.64% due to input and freight costs from the Middle East war.
Working capital: receivables rising faster than revenue; financial cost up about 65% YoY to INR1.53 crores.
Customer concentration: top 10 customers about 70-75% of revenue.
Quebec Petroleum associate acquisition and additional manufacturing unit acquisition: terms and financials not yet disclosed.
Competitive response in Kenya from incumbents such as Shell and Total; payment terms unchanged so far.
Management did not split revenue between manufacturing and toll blending; the reported Q1 PAT decline despite revenue growth needs monitoring.

down from INR2.33 crores in Q1 FY26
up ~INR0.6 crores from INR0.92 crores in Q1 FY26
net profit margin improved to 812 basis points as stated

Our EBITDA margins have shrunk a little bit in terms of percentage. That is due to the increased product cost and increased shipment cost.
And still, even in the given scenario, on a conservative basis, we are estimating that we'll cross around INR 200 crores in the coming means in this financial year with healthy EBITDA margins.

540401|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term demand, scale-up and the FY27 revenue target of crossing about INR200 crores, but guarded on margins, which management attributes to war-driven input and freight costs. Answers were less precise on receivables and on the Quebec Petroleum economics, where deal terms were left for later disclosure.

rows.why: Management says margins will hold or improve through product mix diversification if disruption persists, but Q1 margin was 7.64% versus 9.81% a year ago and receivables and finance costs (INR1.53 crores vs INR0.92 crores) are rising.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.why: Management guides FY27 revenue to cross about INR200 crores, about 8% above FY26's INR184.81 crores, and Q1 revenue rose about 52% YoY to INR59.91 crores, backed by new customers and a Kenya grease plant, though no order book was disclosed.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 45%, well below the 80% threshold, so a fresh capex announcement is not pressed by capacity; but management says capacity suffices for 2-3 years on a single shift and additional storage capex is needed for full use, and an additional manufacturing unit acquisition is in process.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided FY27 revenue above INR200 crores on a conservative basis, only about 8% above FY26's INR184.81 crores, and Q1 revenue grew about 52% YoY, but margin pressure from the war caps any upside to guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin fell to 7.64% from 9.81% (about 217 bps) and PAT dipped to INR2.05 crores from INR2.33 crores on war-driven input and freight costs, and management says margins may dip further if supply disruption lasts beyond six months.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Kenya grease facility is planned for commissioning in Q3 FY27, and the company has broadened product baskets and onboarded new customers, though no specific new product names or dates beyond the grease facility were given.

rows.why: Planned with no capex or timing figures disclosed; manufacturing would follow only once scale is reached.

rows.label: Quebec Petroleum 40% associate stake aimed at India domestic market
rows.why: Proposed acquisition with terms and financials not yet disclosed; associate profits would flow into consolidated numbers once completed.

rows.label: Partial pass-through of war-driven cost increases to selling prices
rows.why: Management has already passed on a partial cost increase, which lifted revenue and receivables, but the margin still fell 217 bps to 7.64%.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term demand, scale-up and the FY27 target of crossing about INR200 crores, but guarded on margins, receivables and Quebec Petroleum economics, which were left for later disclosure.

540403|2026-03.headline: CL Educate revenue rose about 55% to ₹570 crore in FY26 and EBITDA more than doubled to ₹69 crore, driven by the DEXIT acquisition.
540403|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 as the first year the group crossed ₹500 crore revenue, with revenue up from ₹368 crore to ₹570 crore and EBITDA up from ₹33 crore to ₹69 crore. Cash generated from operations rose to ₹79 crore from ₹26 crore, and the acquisition-linked borrowing has been reduced from ₹210 crore to ₹180 crore. The DEXIT (assessments) integration is described as complete. The L&D/EdTech segment remains under structural pressure, with realisations down 12-14% and revenue down about 11%, and management expects it to stay flat for roughly four more quarters. Fundraising has been put on a slight pause.

financial_highlights.change: acquisition debt reduced to ₹180 crore from ₹210 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and bank balance (as on date)
financial_highlights.change: from about ₹50 crore last year, excluding ₹185-190 crore pending RPS redemption

segments.name: Assessments (DEXIT)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose to ₹223 crore from ₹205 crore and EBITDA to about ₹51 crore from ₹34 crore. All existing contracts were rolled over and 20 new customers were added. FY27 order book is about 80-85% of FY26 revenue, per management.

segments.name: L&D / EdTech (test prep, university engagement, publishing)
segments.commentary: Enrollment volume grew about 4% but average realisation fell 12-14%, so revenue declined about 11%. Management expects revenue to stay roughly flat for about four quarters, with profitability improving from Q1 FY27 after cost recalibration.

segments.name: MarTech (Kestone, events, VOSMOS, VIRSA)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 11% to about ₹161 crore: international up about 20%, India up about 5%. EBITDA was slightly lower due to set-up costs for the new social events and luxury wedding business. Domestic to international mix is about 1:2.

guidance_outlook: Assessments: management expects reasonably healthy revenue growth in FY27, backed by an order book of about 80-85% of FY26 revenue six weeks into the year.

MarTech: shift to higher-margin CEP and VOSMOS/VIRSA products over 12-18 months; pruning low-margin MMS and pass-through businesses.
Discontinued operations: bulk of losses done, with a little residual impact possible in Q1 FY27 and none expected beyond that.
Talevate: target to sign 8-10 corporates and about 100 jobs over the next few quarters, testing the MVP before scaling.
capex_capacity: Working capital is about 50% of revenue despite about 50% revenue growth, per management.

Remote proctoring and BYOD technology is being built out at DEXIT; the mySathi IP platform has started going to market.
Settlement of ₹185-190 crore RPS amount awaits NCLT capital reduction approval; order reserved, next hearing on May 15, 2026.
demand_pricing: L&D: enrollment volume up about 4%, but realisation down 12-14%. Students are shifting from ₹30,000-60,000 full programmes to ₹2,000-4,000 modular components.

Assessments: government contracts are about 40-45% of mix and private 55-60%. Pricing is similar across both and the market is price-sensitive.
Assessments: rollover of exam dates by 60-120 days shifted some FY26 revenue into FY27.
Competition: PhysicsWallah-type players are seen as low-price and not a direct threat; management launched products at about 50% above PhysicsWallah pricing and one-third of regular prices.

qa_highlights.question: Does the NEET controversy open opportunities for DEXIT in nationwide exams?
qa_highlights.answer: Yatrik Vin said it is a significant opportunity; DEXIT already conducts exams for IRDAI, ICAI and NISM, and its digital and surveillance tech is ready.

qa_highlights.question: What is the DEXIT government/private mix, contract duration, and government tender criteria?
qa_highlights.answer: Government is about 40-45% and private 55-60%. Contract tenure varies from one to five years, or order-based. RFPs weigh technical at 65-70% and commercial at 30-35%.

qa_highlights.question: How does the order book work, and why is it not 100% revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says 80-85% coverage is in hand for FY27, and sales efforts target a higher rollover. Exam timing set by clients can push revenue into the next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the fundraising plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Satya Narayanan said fundraising is on a slight pause given the environment, and the boards want value at the right valuation. Updates are expected in the next quarter or two.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the cash and current liabilities linked to NSE?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹182 crore was left behind from the NSEIT transition and has earned ₹11-12 crore of interest, so about ₹193-194 crore is on the balance sheet. It will be knocked off against RPS after NCLT approval and moved from non-current to current liabilities.

qa_highlights.question: How will VIRSA affect MarTech in North America?
qa_highlights.answer: Pilots with Salesforce, Dell and Infosys have had positive feedback. The Salesforce work is for Canada, with a scale-up to the US expected over the next couple of quarters.

Assessment revenue timing depends on client exam schedules, which have rolled over by 60-120 days before.

540403|2026-06.headline: CL Educate Q1 FY27: revenue fell about ₹17.5 crore QoQ-type decline offset by ₹18 crore cost cuts, lifting EBITDA margin ~218 bps to 16.6%, though still loss-making after tax.
540403|2026-06.overview: Management said Q1 revenue was weak, with a decline of about ₹17.5 crore on a full-quarter basis, but operational and overhead cost cuts of about ₹18 crore (₹9.3 crore service delivery, ₹8.7 crore fixed overheads) kept EBITDA marginally above Q1 FY26 and margin at about 16.6%. After-tax profit remained negative due to interest and depreciation. Test prep (EdTech L&D) revenue fell about 15% to ₹45 crore from ₹53 crore amid MBA market churn, while DEX digital assessments revenue fell about 17% on a base effect and ₹4.7 crore of deferred revenue. Management framed Q1 as the seasonally weakest quarter and guided to Q2 and Q3 recovery for MarTech and DEX.

financial_highlights.change: up about 218 bps YoY (call also cites ~340 bps in EdTech context)

financial_highlights.value: about ₹18 crore (₹9.3 crore service delivery + ₹8.7 crore fixed overheads)

financial_highlights.change: down ~15% from ₹53 crore; EBITDA down ~13%, margin up ~60 bps

segments.name: EdTech – Test Prep (L&D)

segments.name: DEX – Digital Assessments
segments.commentary: Revenue down ~17% YoY; EBITDA down ~4.3%. Drivers: ~₹6 crore rollover exams in Q1 FY26 and ₹4.7 crore revenue pending customer result declarations, expected in Q2. Won nine contracts worth ~₹34 crore TCV, ~₹22 crore to execute this year.

segments.name: MarTech
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~₹7 crore (about 3.8%-7% cited); EBITDA up ~32-35%; margin up ~180 bps. Technology business ~10% of revenue last year, targeted at 13-15% this year. Q2 is largest season.

qa_highlights.question: How will exam rationalisation and the NTA/Nilekani task force affect DEX, and what is its near and medium term growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects exam digitisation and consolidation (possibly into SAT/GMAT/GRE-like exams) with some opportunities emerging and others disappearing; timing is 12-24 months and too early to quantify. Management sees enrolment growth of ~60% over nine years as expanding the addressable market.

qa_highlights.question: Could NTA build in-house proctoring software to mitigate malpractice, and how does DEX compare?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued few players have DEX-level secure, AI-enabled, real-time remote proctoring with control-room monitoring, and sees tighter scrutiny as an opportunity for credible providers.

qa_highlights.question: How is BBA/IPM performing in test prep, and what is the impact of PhysicsWallah's AI content?
qa_highlights.answer: Gautam Puri said BBA/IPM is a growth segment with more five-year programmes, and that AI content generation has been in use for 1.5-2 years; PhysicsWallah targets the lower end while CL focuses on mid-to-upper segments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt reduction plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Target to be near net-zero debt within 36 months; scheduled repayments on track; acquisition loan reduced from ₹210 crore to ₹174 crore. Accelerated repayment possible if surplus cash arises, but MarTech and DEX need cash for expansion.

qa_highlights.question: How does DEX pricing work and how sensitive is it to price changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing is per seat/candidate; over 60% of business is government tenders awarded on techno-commercial basis, where CL usually wins on technology (T1) but can lose on lowest price (L1).

qa_highlights.question: How is VIRSA progressing in Singapore and North America?

540403|2026-09.headline: CL Educate H1 FY27 EBITDA rose to ~₹57 crore (margin ~18.6% vs 15.7%) on 4% revenue decline to ₹305 crore, with PAT back positive.
540403|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 revenue fell about 4% to ₹305 crore from ₹319 crore, driven by EdTech (down ~13%) and DEXIT base effects from rollover contracts in Q1 FY26. Cost actions cut overheads by about ₹12.5 crore, lifting EBITDA from ~₹50 crore to ~₹57 crore and margin about 3 percentage points, with PAT returning to positive (up ~350%). Management flagged ~₹172 crore of new multi-year DEXIT contract wins, of which ~₹40 crore accrues in FY27, and a pending DEXIT merger into CL Educate. Overall tone was upbeat on H2 but the call gave few hard forward numbers.

CL Media (platform monetisation) flat in H1, with admission-cycle seasonality shifting to start in October.

segments.commentary: Revenue down ~8% (about ₹10-11 crore), mainly due to Q1 FY26 rollover contracts not recurring; Q2 roughly flat vs Q1. EBITDA down ~2% in absolute terms with margin up ~171 bps. qa_highlights.question: Tax and other savings from the DEXIT merger, timeline, and route?
