rows.why: First PPP disbursement (Dharavi) expected in Q3 from about INR9,000 crore of PPP sanctions, but no new product launch was specifically guided.

rows.label: Borrower repricing pass-through of higher costs
rows.why: About INR20,000 crore of loans reset in H1 and a 15 bps MCLR increase reflects in Q3 FY27, with management saying yields will rise over the next two quarters against bonds around 8%.

rows.label: ECB borrowing under RBI swap window
rows.why: About INR35,000 crore of ECB at about 6.5%-6.75% is expected before the window closes, targeting slightly above $3 billion, which should cap funding costs.

rows.label: Negative credit costs from provision reversals
rows.why: Provision coverage around 95% and gross NPA about 0.7% (net NPA 0.04%) support reversals for one to two years, though sustainability is uncertain.

tone.note: Management was confident on disbursement growth, asset quality and the 2% spread and 3% NIM targets, but cautious on cost of funds, repricing lag and PPP timing; analysts pushed on how spreads hold up without relief in funding costs.

540544|2026-03.headline: PSP Projects Q4FY26 revenue rose 66% YoY to INR1,115 crores, but a INR29 crore Kashi ECL provision kept FY26 PAT flat at INR55 crores.
540544|2026-03.overview: Q4FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR1,115 crores (up 66% YoY), with EBITDA up 85% to INR60 crores and PAT up to INR21 crores. Reported margins were depressed by a INR29 crore expected credit loss provision on unbilled revenue from the Kashi project, which took other expenses from INR17 crores to INR46 crores. For FY26, revenue grew 25% to INR3,149 crores, EBITDA rose 5% to INR189 crores with margin down to 6% from 7.14%, and PAT was flat-to-down at INR55 crores. Order book reached INR13,447 crores (up 85%) after record order inflow of INR10,925 crores, 85% of it from the Adani group.

segments.name: Adani group (in-house) orders
segments.commentary: Adani group accounted for 85% of FY26 order inflow and about INR9,000 crores (67%) of the current INR13,400 crore order book. Management says materials are pass-through on Adani contracts.

segments.name: External / non-group orders
segments.commentary: External projects are about 33-43% of the order book (about INR4,300 crores per the Q&A). Government projects fell to about 25% of the order book from 43% a year earlier.

segments.name: Precast manufacturing
segments.commentary: Current precast capacity is 3 million sq ft per year. Management says expansion to 1.5x would need only INR15-20 crores of equipment since sheds are already built. Project 90 was pre-executed in 148 days.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance is about INR4,500 crores, reiterated by management.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 7-8%, with management saying it can move 1% plus or minus; the Q&A confirmed 7-8% as the band for the next two years.
Management expects to be debt-free within about two to three quarters, with interest cost of about INR11-12 crores per quarter falling toward nil.
Working capital: trade receivable days are expected to fall to about 60 days (60-70 days per the Q&A) from about 94 days.

Order inflow is expected at INR5,000-6,000 crores from the group plus INR1,000-2,000 crores from outside in FY27. The bid pipeline is about INR6,500 crores, of which about INR5,000 crores is group and INR1,500 crores external.
Capex for FY27 is expected at about INR120-150 crores (roughly 2-4% of revenue), with quarterly lumpiness possible.
Employee cost is expected to grow about 2-4% (per the Q&A), with operating leverage as revenue rises.
Medium-term goal is 20-25% growth per year, with a target of about INR9,000-10,000 crores revenue by FY30 (per the analyst's recap, not restated by management).
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was INR192 crores; Q4FY26 capex was INR40 crores. Gross block is INR764 crores and net block INR412 crores.
Precast plant capacity is 3 million sq ft per year; management sees no major expansion needed at the current pace.
Projects under execution: 94 ongoing across Gujarat, UP, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Delhi NCR; over 256 completed to date.

Mumbai projects (Mahim, Matunga) are at early foundation stage; Matunga is at sheet piling. Tree-cutting approvals are a delay risk. Management says about INR10,000 crores of the order book is at peak execution pace.
Dharoi Dam Phase 1 was handed over and Phase 2 is in finishing. SMC RCC is complete and RVNL core and shell is complete.
demand_pricing: Order book INR13,447 crores (+85% YoY), with group projects at 67% and external at 43% per the CEO's figures (these overlap; the Q&A split is 67% Adani and 33% non-Adani).
Record FY26 order inflow of INR10,925 crores, 85% from Adani group. Major wins include SVPI Airport Ahmedabad development, Matunga Rehab Building Mumbai, and Shri Ambaji Mata Temple extension.

Key outstanding orders: Shree Ambaji Mata Temple INR966 crores, SMC Highrise INR731 crores, Human & Biological Science Gallery INR254 crores, GIFT City Fintech Building INR261 crores, Dharoi Dam INR223 crores, Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya INR216 crores, Sabarmati Riverfront Phase II INR218 crores, GIFT City residential INR210 crores.

Commonwealth Games-linked tenders (about INR7,000-8,000 crores potential, per analyst) are expected to be announced but had not been formally released; management expects them 'anytime in this quarter'.
Mobilisation advances of INR814 crores from the group are interest-free. Management says the group advance will fund most working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue guidance of INR4,500 crores and FY30 target of INR9,000-10,000 crores changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management stuck to INR4,500 crores for FY27 and said margins are improving; Q4 EBITDA margin excluding the INR30 crore provision would be about 8%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kashi ECL provision and will more come?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR29 crore provision was made because receivables beyond one year must be provided for. Management is still chasing the UP Medical College accounts through government channels and does not expect major further ECL provisions.

qa_highlights.question: How much UP Medical College money is outstanding?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR60 crores unbilled and INR40 crores trade receivable across seven projects. INR40 crores of GST invoices are pending, and final certification is awaited.

qa_highlights.question: Will PAT margin reach 4-5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to be debt-free within about two to three quarters, which would remove about INR41-45 crores of annual interest. It said PAT margin could reach 3-4% and that 4.5-5% is the target for next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook and receivable days?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days were about 90-100 at March 2026 because most revenue was booked in February and March. Management expects them to fall to around 60-70 days, with collection in April.

qa_highlights.question: Is capex/depreciation going to stay at 3% of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 capex is about INR120-150 crores, with possible flexibility to about 2% of revenue. Depreciation is expected to keep rising from new assets, so it cannot be cut.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SDB receivable status?
qa_highlights.answer: The client has just started operations. About INR90 crores of principal is in receivables, with interest billed separately. Management expects resolution during FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Adani mix or the ongoing war pressure margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most orders are Adani with pass-through materials, so it sees no major war-related margin risk. Only SMC and RVNL may see small impact.

risks_watch: Receivables jumped to INR928 crores (about 90-100 days) at March 2026; watch April-June collections against management's 60-70 day target.
Collection risk on UP Medical College (about INR60 crores unbilled and INR40 crores receivable) and the remaining Kashi and SDB balances. Further ECL provisions are possible.
Margin guidance (7-8%) depends on no further provisions. Q4 margin was depressed by the INR29 crore provision, and FY26 EBITDA margin fell to 6%.
Concentration risk: about 67% of the order book is Adani group. Mobilisation advances of INR814 crores are a funding source; a slowdown in group inflows would matter.
Execution risk in Mumbai (tree-cutting approvals, monsoon, labour availability in Q1-Q2 FY27), and the timing of Commonwealth-linked tenders.
Debt-free target and interest saving depend on collections; gross debt of about INR317 crores (INR43 crores long-term plus INR274 crores short-term) remains.

540544|2026-06.headline: PSP Projects Q1 FY27 revenue rose 65% YoY to INR853 crores, with order book at INR13,245 crores (up 103% YoY) and EBITDA margin of 6.42%.
540544|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 65% YoY to INR853 crores and EBITDA rose 121% to INR55 crores, with margin expanding to 6.42% from 4.79%. Net profit reached INR18 crores versus INR37 lakhs a year earlier. Management attributed the margin shortfall versus its 7-8% target to weak April-May billing against labour-heavy costs, with employee cost at 5.4% of sales. Management reiterated FY27 revenue of INR4,400-4,500 crores and a 7-8% EBITDA margin for the full year, with the bulk of improvement expected in the second half.

segments.name: Order book by sector
segments.commentary: Industrial 39%, residential 37%, government 23%, institutional about 1%. Q1 order inflow was INR630 crores, 93% from Adani Group.

segments.name: Precast

qa_highlights.question: Will the company be net debt-free within two to three quarters?

qa_highlights.question: Is there a Dharavi opportunity beyond the current two projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it holds the first right of refusal. Further projects depend on performance on the current two. Redevelopment of about 2 lakh houses over roughly five to six years is planned, with separate development of cleared land after that.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate outlook?

qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost-plus contracts work out to about 7% EBITDA, with a 1-2% gap depending on location (Mumbai about 3%, Mundra about 1.5%).

540544|2026-09.headline: PSP Projects Q2 FY27 revenue rose 58% YoY to INR1,113 crore, with EBITDA up 38% to INR69 crore and PAT up 87% to INR30 crore.
540544|2026-09.overview: Management reported record quarterly and half-year revenue, with Q2 revenue of INR1,113 crore (+58% YoY) and H1 revenue of INR1,967 crore (+61% YoY). Q2 EBITDA margin was 6.21% versus 7.10% in the comparable quarter, while H1 EBITDA margin was 6.30% versus 6.12% in H1 FY26. Order book stood at INR12,872 crore (+30% YoY) and H1 order inflow was about INR1,305 crore, including INR675 crore in Q2. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth guidance of 30-35% (commitment at the lower end) while saying it internally targets growth above 30%, and kept H2 margin commentary toward about 7%.

financial_highlights.change: +38% YoY vs INR50 crore; margin vs 7.10% in prior comparable quarter

financial_highlights.value: INR62 crore in Q2; INR91 crore in H1

segments.name: External projects

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for order inflow for the remaining months, and whether bid pipeline implies INR3,000-4,000 crore wins?

qa_highlights.question: How are cost inflation and working capital handled on Adani projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Adani is cost-plus with material differences reimbursed; workforce costs adjusted about 10%; about 75% of bills cleared in 7-10 days, so working capital challenge is limited.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin below 7.5-8% guidance from last quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most projects are in RCC structure stage where overhead absorption is low; margins should improve as the 70% finishing scope with MEP and interiors runs faster over 6-7 months.

qa_highlights.question: Capex guidance and unbilled revenue normalisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex about INR100 crore more in H2 FY27 and 3-4% of revenue thereafter; unbilled rose because government bills for last month are pending certification and GST invoicing, and management expects normalisation depending on project type.

qa_highlights.question: Surat Diamond Bourse and UP receivables status?
qa_highlights.answer: No commitment yet on SDB (about INR90 crore stays outstanding). UP receivables: INR810 crore received from pool plus about INR20-25 crore out of about INR40 crore; remaining expected by Q3 FY27.

risks_watch: Margin sustainability: H1 EBITDA margin 6.30% and Q2 6.21% are below the ~7% full-year target; analysts flagged that the Adani business margin (about 5.5-5.7% per an analyst) may cap blended margins.
Unbilled revenue at INR632 crore and trade receivables at INR809 crore; management noted government bill certification and GST invoicing delays each quarter.

Expected credit loss provision of about INR8 crore in Q2 (INR8.1 crore doubtful advances per analyst), with management saying ECL of INR3-4 crore is normal annually; an analyst estimated adjusted margin near 6.7%.
Order inflow pace: H1 at INR1,305 crore is well below the INR4,000-6,000 crore full-year expectations discussed on the call.
Receivables from Surat Diamond Bourse (about INR90 crore) have no committed payment timeline.
Labour availability and cost inflation (war-related material price increases noted on SMC and RVNL projects), and Adani concentration of about 72-75% of the order book.
Mobilisation advance INR933 crore, high relative to inventory and receivables; need to watch execution of interior and MEP phases on large projects.

Answers on Adani economics and receivables were more evasive, with no segment revenue split and no firm SDB payment timeline.
key_quotes: PSP Projects delivered its highest ever quarter and half yearly revenue.

Our order book is almost 75% is Adani and 25% is non-Adani.

rows.why: Material differences are reimbursed and workforce costs are adjusted about 10%, with overall cost impact around 7%, which supports margin stability on about 72-75% of the book.

540575|2026-03.headline: Star Cement Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose to INR324 crore (INR1,871/t) and FY26 PAT more than doubled to INR390 crore; FY27 cement volume guided up 10-12%.
540575|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was about INR1,174 crore vs INR1,052 crore a year ago, with EBITDA excluding exceptional items of INR324 crore vs INR268 crore and PAT of INR147 crore vs INR123 crore. Cement sales rose to 16.18 lakh tonnes from 14.75 lakh tonnes, while clinker sales jumped to 1.15 lakh tonnes from 0.57 lakh tonnes. For FY26, EBITDA was INR955 crore (INR1,738/t) vs INR589 crore (INR1,245/t), and PAT was INR390 crore vs INR169 crore. Management flagged April-May demand softness from state elections, a near-term fuel and packing cost hit of INR250-300 crore in H1 FY27, and a lower subsidy run-rate in FY27.

segments.name: Northeast cement
segments.commentary: Q4 Northeast sales were about 11.27 lakh tonnes vs 11.02 lakh tonnes a year ago. Management guides Northeast EBITDA at INR1,500-1,700/t over the next 2-3 years, on a full-year basis.

segments.name: Outside Northeast cement
segments.commentary: Q4 sales were 4.91 lakh tonnes vs 3.74 lakh tonnes a year ago, about 31% growth. Management said trade share was about 78% vs 81% a year ago.

segments.name: Clinker
segments.commentary: Q4 clinker sales were 1.15 lakh tonnes vs 0.57 lakh tonnes. FY27 clinker volumes are expected to be flat at about 3.5 lakh tonnes, with the focus on realisation rather than volume.

segments.name: Non-cement (AAC blocks, RMC)
segments.commentary: Q4 non-cement revenue was about INR17 crore and FY26 was about INR43 crore. FY27 target is about INR150 crore at a 7-8% margin to start.

guidance_outlook: FY27 cement volume growth of 10-12% on about 5.3 million tonnes achieved in FY26 (excludes clinker).
FY27 subsidy income expected to fall by INR40-50 crore vs FY26's INR184 crore, to about INR140-150 crore.
Q1 FY27 fuel cost rise of INR0.15-0.20 per GCV for coal, with the impact expected to ease by June; estimated H1 FY27 cost impact of INR250-300 crore from packing and fuel.
Capex of INR600-700 crore in FY27 and about INR1,500 crore in FY28, contingent on approvals expected by October.
Q1 FY27 EBITDA will face pressure; management expects the Northeast EBITDA/t guidance to hold on a full-year average.
capex_capacity: Nimbol (Rajasthan) clinker plant of about 3.3 million tonnes, plus 2-2.5 million tonnes grinding there and 2-2.5 million tonnes grinding in Haryana; the Rajasthan setup totals about 5 million tonnes of cement capacity. Target start about September 2028 to 1H FY29.

Bihar greenfield grinding unit of about 2 million tonnes, expected 1Q-2Q FY29, supplied with clinker from Meghalaya via Silchar rail siding. Bihar FCSC incentive of 150-200% of investment applied for.
Umrangso (Assam) clinker plant and Jorhat grinding unit (about 2 million tonnes, grinding only), to follow over 4-5 years.
Three-project capex total cited at about INR4,800 crore; the investor presentation will carry a year-wise capex split in about a week.
Clinker factor (CC ratio) was 66.2% in Q4, and management estimates the FY26 ratio at 66.6-67.5%.
demand_pricing: April demand was sluggish due to Assam and West Bengal elections; management sees a pickup in May.
Pricing: Northeast up about INR6-7 per bag and outside Northeast (West Bengal, Bihar) up about INR10 per bag vs the March exit.
Premium cement share was 15.1% in Q4; blend mix was 18% OPC and the rest PPC.
Lead distance fell to about 220 km from 229 km a year ago; KKL cost was about INR1.24 per GCV.
Management expects a new mainland entrant to take 3-4 years; it expects price pressure for 1-2 years after entry, then normalisation.
Green share was about 33.8% in Q4; management guides 30-33% for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 volume guidance and the April-May demand trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guides 10-12% cement volume growth on about 5.3 million tonnes. April was sluggish due to elections, with a pickup in May; it will refine the estimate after June.

qa_highlights.question: How much will subsidies fall in FY27, and what is the capex outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidies fall by INR40-50 crore to about INR140-150 crore. Capex is INR600-700 crore in FY27 and about INR1,500 crore in FY28, subject to approvals by October.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost impact of fuel and packing from the West Asia situation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates an H1 FY27 impact of INR250-300 crore, mainly packing and fuel, with prices partly offset by hikes of INR7 in Northeast and INR10 in North Bengal. Q1 EBITDA will be under pressure, with June expected to normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt and cash position?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt is INR583 crore and net debt is INR200 crore, implying cash and liquid investments of about INR383 crore. The non-current investment rise reflects liquid bonds with maturities under one year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Rajasthan and Haryana plant breakevens and realisation targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 80-90% utilisation in 3.5-4 years and prices about INR5-10 below the highest-priced seller. It gave no explicit breakeven year and framed the strategy around brand building and dense distribution.

qa_highlights.question: How will new mainland entrants affect Northeast profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Tushar Bhajanka expects significant pressure once they enter, which may last 1-2 years before normalising. He says Star Cement has the highest trade penetration among Northeast players.

540575|2026-06.headline: Star Cement Q1 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR203 crore (INR1,497/t) from INR230 crore, with PAT at INR74 crore versus INR98 crore on subsidy cuts and fuel costs.
540575|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue rose to about INR902 crore from INR847 crore, but EBITDA declined to INR203 crore and EBITDA per tonne dropped to INR1,497 from INR1,774. Management attributed the fall to lower Assam incentive accruals (GST cut from 28% to 18%), higher packing and fuel costs, and a kiln shutdown. Cement volumes grew about 7% to 13.02 lakh tonnes, but Northeast volume was flat, and management cut FY27 cement volume growth guidance to 8-9% from 11-12%. Management also updated the Rajasthan (Nimbol) and Haryana (Jhajjar) expansion plan, with capex now about INR2,700 crore (INR2,900 crore incl. GST).

segments.name: Northeast cement
segments.commentary: Sold about 8.71 lakh tonnes vs 8.67 lakh tonnes YoY, essentially flat; management attributed the weakness to April Assam elections and monsoon, not competition.

segments.name: Outside Northeast (Bihar, West Bengal)
segments.commentary: Sold 4.31 lakh tonnes vs 3.55 lakh tonnes YoY (up ~21%), the main volume growth driver this quarter.

segments.name: Building Solutions (AAC, RMC)
segments.commentary: Management said the INR150 crore revenue target is a revenue (not EBITDA) estimate; current run-rate is below it, with ARR expected to reach that level by Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 cement volume growth revised to 8-9% from 11-12%; Northeast growth target 8-9% vs industry about 7%.
FY27 clinker sales expected flat to down 5-10% vs FY26 as clinker is now sourced externally in the Northeast.
Q2 FY27 EBITDA per tonne guided at about INR1,400, with INR1,500-1,600 for the full year.
Fuel cost guided to fall from INR1.55/kcal-equivalent in Q1 to about INR1.45 in Q2 and lower in Q3-Q4 (CFO/MD cited Q4 FY26 at INR1.33).
Assam incentive for FY27 revised to about INR115 crore from earlier INR145 crore due to new equated payout rules.

Cost savings of INR60-70 crore expected in Q2 vs Q1 from lower one-off donation and incentive items; further savings from Silchar railway siding (Oct-Nov), Siliguri wagon tippler (about INR150/t saving on Siliguri sales), and EVs over 5-6 months.
Expects double-digit volume growth in Q3-Q4 FY27 once flood waters recede, with pent-up demand.
Subsidy drag expected to end after September 2026, as GST cut base effect rolls off.
capex_capacity: Rajasthan (Nimbol) integrated plant: 3.0 million tonnes grinding and 3.3 million tonnes clinker; public hearing in August, EC expected by early October, groundwork from mid-October to November; commissioning in about 18-20 months (Q4 FY28 to Q1 FY29).
Jhajjar (Haryana) plant of 2 million tonnes; total expansion capex about INR2,700 crore (about INR2,900 crore including GST), vs earlier INR2,250 crore Nimbol plus about INR650 crore Haryana.
Q1 FY27 capex spend about INR93 crore; FY27 capex guidance of INR500 crore unchanged; FY28 capex about INR1,500 crore.

West Bengal grinding decision pending the state industrial policy (expected around 15 August): may redirect the 2 million tonne Bihar (Begusarai) grinding capex to a Siliguri brownfield unit, though a single 1 million tonne unit may not be economic.

Packing (PP bag) costs up due to international war-driven crude price increase; management said these are hard to predict.
Premium (PPC/OPC) share about 15.9%; trade share about 80%; lead distance about 210 km; clinker factor about 66.5%; green share about 3% including WHRS.
Fuel mix Q1: FSA about 45%, spot coal about 30%, balance biomass and others; coal diverted to power plants limited FSA rake availability.
Sand mining crackdown in West Bengal has weighed on regional cement demand.
Management said Sept 2025 base was weak due to GST cut, so September 2026 should show easier comparison.

qa_highlights.question: Will volume growth improve in Q2 and what is FY27 volume outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 volume growth is limited by Assam floods; management now expects FY27 cement growth of 8-9% vs earlier 11-12%, with double-digit growth in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is INR1,500/t EBITDA sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes over the full year (INR1,500-1,600/t), but Q2 is guided to about INR1,400/t due to shutdown costs and rain-hit fixed-cost absorption.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rajasthan timeline and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: EC expected by October, construction from November, commissioning in 18-20 months; combined Rajasthan and Haryana capex about INR2,700 crore (INR2,900 crore with GST).

qa_highlights.question: Is a QIP planned and what leverage is targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: No active QIP plan; management targets about 1.5-1.6x net debt/EBITDA to fund expansion, with QIP considered only for opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: How much is outstanding from the Assam government on incentives?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR130 crore outstanding; total scheme value INR794 crore, now paid over 12 years, reducing FY27 expected receipts to about INR115 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a Northeast market share or competition concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no market share loss and that the Q1 dip reflects elections and monsoon, not Dalmia's capacity ramp.
